name: 1 Enoch
sourceNote: Translated from the Ethiopic (Ge‘ez) text of 1 Enoch as edited by R. H. Charles, *The Ethiopic Version of the Book of Enoch* (1906), with his revised translation-base of 1912, and A. Dillmann, *Liber Henoch aethiopice* (1851), both public domain. The Greek witnesses were compared where they survive: the Akhmim (Panopolitanus) codex for chapters 1–32, the excerpts in George Syncellus for parts of chapters 6–16, and the Chester Beatty–Michigan papyrus for chapters 97–107, as printed by Swete (1891–94), Charles (1912), and Flemming and Radermacher (1901). The Aramaic fragments from Qumran Cave 4 (4QEnᵃ⁻ᵍ and 4QEnastrᵃ⁻ᵈ, about 200 BC to the turn of the era) cover parts of every section except the Parables (chapters 37–71); readings from them are cited as reported in the standard editions and have not been checked against the manuscripts. R. H. Charles’s 1913 English translation (public domain) was consulted, but the English here is new. Ge‘ez *Egzi’abḥer* is rendered “the Lord” and *Amlāk* “God”; the divine name Yahweh does not appear in any surviving text of 1 Enoch, which prefers titles such as “the Great Holy One,” “the Lord of Spirits,” and “the Most High,” so it is not supplied here. **About the book.** 1 Enoch is a collection of five books ascribed to Enoch, the seventh from Adam (Gen 5:18–24): the Book of the Watchers (chapters 1–36, 3rd century BC), the Book of Parables or Similitudes (37–71, probably late 1st century BC or 1st century AD), the Astronomical Book (72–82, 3rd century BC or earlier), the Book of Dreams (83–90, about 165–160 BC), and the Epistle of Enoch (91–108, 2nd century BC), with an appendix on the birth of Noah (106–107) and a closing exhortation (108). It was composed in Aramaic (perhaps partly Hebrew), translated into Greek, and from Greek into Ge‘ez, probably in the 5th–6th centuries AD; the complete book survives only in Ethiopic manuscripts, the oldest from about the 15th century. The Letter of Jude quotes 1 Enoch 1:9 as a prophecy of “Enoch, the seventh from Adam” (Jude 14–15), and several early Christian writers valued the book. It is part of the Old Testament of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church and the Eritrean Orthodox Church, and of the Scriptures of Beta Israel; it is not in the canon of other Jewish or Christian communities. Verse numbering follows Charles. Chapters 91–93 are printed in the Ethiopic order; the Aramaic copy 4QEnᵍ reportedly places 91:11–17 after 93:1–10, which restores the “Apocalypse of Weeks” to its natural sequence (see the notes there). Calendar dates are given with modern-month equivalents and clock-like divisions are explained in notes, according to the CJT conventions.

verses.text: The words of blessing of Enoch,{a} with which he blessed the chosen{b} and the righteous who will be living in the day of distress, when all the wicked and the godless are to be removed.

He took up his discourse{c} and said: Enoch was a righteous man; God opened his eyes, and he saw a vision of the Holy One in heaven, which the angels showed me. From them I heard everything, and from them I understood what I saw, not for this generation but for one far off that is yet to come.

Concerning the chosen I spoke, and I took up my discourse about them:
The Great Holy One{d} will come out from his dwelling,

All will be struck with fear,
and the Watchers{g} will tremble,
and great fear and shaking will seize them to the ends of the earth.

notes.text: *Enoch*: Hebrew *Ḥanokh*, probably “dedicated” or “initiated.” He is the son of Jared and the seventh from Adam, who “walked with God” and was taken by God (Gen 5:18–24).
Chosen: Ge‘ez *ḥeruyān*, traditionally “the elect”; so throughout the book.
Discourse: Ge‘ez *messālē*, Greek *parabolē*, Aramaic *matla*: a solemn oracle or figurative speech, traditionally “parable.” So throughout.
The Great Holy One: so the Greek; the Ethiopic has “the Holy and Great One.” The Aramaic fragments reportedly use *qaddisha rabba*, “the Great Holy One,” a favorite title for God in this book.
Mount Sinai: compare Deut 33:2; Mic 1:3.
He will appear with his host: so the Greek, “he will appear out of his camp”; Charles regarded the line as a doublet of the next.
Watchers: Aramaic *‘irin*, “wakeful ones,” a class of angels (Dan 4:13, 17, 23). In this book the word usually refers to the angels who sinned (chapters 6–16).
Split wide apart: so the Greek; the Ethiopic reads “sink.”
Myriads of his holy ones: literally “ten thousands.” This verse is quoted in Jude 14–15. A fragment of the Aramaic (4QEnᶜ) reportedly preserves part of it.

verses.text: Consider everything that takes place in the sky: how the lights in the heavens do not change their paths, how each rises and sets in order at its own time and does not depart from its appointed law.
Look at the earth and pay attention to the things that happen on it from first to last: how steady they are, how nothing on earth changes, but all the works of God appear before you.
Consider summer and winter: in them the whole earth is full of water, and cloud, dew, and rain lie over it.

Observe and see how in winter every tree appears dried up, having dropped all its leaves, except fourteen trees that do not lose their foliage but keep the old leaves for two or three years until the new ones come.{a}

notes.text: Fourteen trees: so the Ethiopic; the Greek is lost here. The number may come from a list of evergreens in the Aramaic original, now lost.

verses.text: Observe again the days of summer, how the sun stands over the earth opposite it. You look for shade and shelter because of the heat of the sun, and the earth too burns with scorching heat, so that you cannot walk on the ground or on a rock because of its heat.
Observe how the trees clothe themselves with green leaves and bear fruit. So pay attention and understand all his works, and recognize that he who lives forever made them this way.
All his works go on in this way from year to year forever, and all the tasks that they perform for him; their tasks do not change, but everything is done as God has ordained.
See how the sea and the rivers likewise perform their tasks and do not depart from his commands.

But you have not stood firm,
and you have not done the commandments of the Lord.
You have turned aside and spoken proud and harsh words
with your unclean mouths against his greatness.
You hard-hearted, you will find no peace!

Therefore you will curse your days,
and the years of your life will perish;
the years of your destruction will be multiplied in an everlasting curse,
and you will find no mercy.

For the chosen there will be light and grace and peace,
and they will inherit the earth.

Then wisdom will be given to the chosen,
and they will all live and never sin again,
neither through godlessness nor through pride;
but those who have wisdom will be humble.

They will not go wrong again,
nor will they sin all the days of their life,
nor will they die from anger or wrath,
but they will complete the number of the days of their life.
Their lives will grow long in peace,
and the years of their joy will be many,
in everlasting gladness and peace,
all the days of their life.

notes.text: The righteous: this word is missing in the Ethiopic, which leaves a gap here; it is supplied from the sense and the Greek.

verses.text: Now when the human race had multiplied, in those days beautiful and lovely daughters were born to them.
The angels, the sons of heaven,{a} saw them and desired them, and they said to one another, “Come, let us choose wives for ourselves from the daughters of men and father children for ourselves.”
Shemihazah,{b} who was their leader, said to them, “I fear that you will not really agree to do this deed, and I alone will have to pay the penalty for a great sin.”
They all answered him, “Let us all swear an oath and bind ourselves by curses on one another not to give up this plan, but to carry it out.”
Then they all swore together and bound themselves by curses on one another to it.

They numbered two hundred in all, and in the days of Jared they descended{c} onto the peak of Mount Hermon.{d} They named it Mount Hermon because on it they had taken the oath and put themselves under curses.

These are the names of their leaders: Shemihazah, their leader; Arteqoph,{e} Ramtel, Kokabel, Tamiel, Ramiel, Danel, Ziqiel, Baraqel, Asael, Armaros, Batriel, Ananel, Zeqiel, Shamshiel, Sahriel, Turiel, Yomiel, and Sariel.
These are their chiefs over tens.{f}

notes.text: Sons of heaven: the angels; compare “sons of God” in Gen 6:2. Chapters 6–11 retell Gen 6:1–4.
*Shemihazah*: so the Aramaic and Greek; Ethiopic *Semyāzā*. The name probably means “the Name has seen” or “my name has seen.”
*Jared*: Hebrew *Yered*, “descent,” the father of Enoch (Gen 5:15–18). The book plays on the name: in his days the angels “descended.”
Hermon: the mountain is named from a root meaning “ban” or “devote under oath” (*ḥerem*); hence the wordplay with the curse-oath that they swore there. Compare Jubilees 4:15.

The names are given in the Aramaic forms where these are reported from the fragments, otherwise in the Greek or Ethiopic forms; the Ethiopic spellings are badly corrupted. Most are formed with *-el*, “God,” and a word for a natural phenomenon or skill. *Arteqoph* (Ethiopic *Arākiba*): “earth of the mighty one” (uncertain). *Ramtel* (Ethiopic *Rāmē’ēl*): “burning ash of God.” *Kokabel*: “star of God.” *Tamiel*: “perfection of God” (uncertain). *Ramiel*: “thunder of God” or “exalted of God.” *Danel*: “God has judged.” *Ziqiel* (Ethiopic *Ezeqeel*): “lightning flash of God.” *Baraqel*: “lightning of God.” *Asael*: “God has made.” *Armaros*: perhaps from *Hermoni*, “the one of Hermon.” *Batriel*: “rain of God” (uncertain). *Ananel*: “cloud of God.” *Zeqiel* (Ethiopic *Zaqiel*): “sparks of God.” *Shamshiel* (Ethiopic *Samsapeel*): “sun of God.” *Sahriel* (Ethiopic *Satarel*): “moon of God.” *Turiel*: “mountain of God.” *Yomiel*: “day of God.” *Sariel* (Ethiopic) or *Yehaddiel* (reported Aramaic): meaning uncertain.
Chiefs over tens: each of the twenty leaders (counting Shemihazah) commanded ten of the two hundred.

verses.text: These, and all the others with them, took wives for themselves; each chose one for himself, and they began to go in to them and to defile themselves with them. They taught them sorcery and spells, and the cutting of roots, and showed them plants.{a}
The women became pregnant and bore great giants, whose height was three thousand cubits.{b}
They consumed everything that people had produced, and when people could no longer support them,
the giants turned against them and devoured human beings.
They began to sin against the birds, the animals, the creeping things, and the fish, and to devour one another’s flesh, and they drank the blood.
Then the earth brought an accusation against the lawless ones.

notes.text: Plants: that is, the use of herbs for magic and medicine.

Three thousand cubits: about 4,500 feet (1,350 m), reckoning the cubit at 18 inches (45 cm). The Ethiopic has “ells” (cubits); some Greek witnesses, in Syncellus, add that the giants fathered Nephilim, and the Nephilim fathered the Eliud.

verses.text: Asael{a} taught people to make swords and knives, shields and breastplates. He showed them the metals of the earth and how to work them, and bracelets and ornaments, the use of antimony{b} and the painting of the eyelids, all kinds of precious stones, and all coloring dyes.
There was a great deal of godlessness; they committed sexual immorality, they were led astray, and they became corrupt in all their ways.

Shemihazah taught spells and the cutting of roots; Armaros, the undoing of spells; Baraqel, the reading of lightning; Kokabel, the signs of the stars; Ziqiel, the signs of the flashes; Arteqoph, the signs of the earth; Shamshiel, the signs of the sun; and Sahriel, the courses of the moon.{c}
As people were perishing, they cried out, and their cry went up to heaven.

notes.text: *Asael*: so the Aramaic, reportedly, and the Greek (*Asaēl*), one of the leaders listed at 6:7; the Ethiopic has *Azazel* here and elsewhere, the name of the figure in the Day of Atonement ritual (Lev 16:8–10), and the two figures were merged in the tradition. *Asael* means “God has made.”
Antimony: a black powder used as eye paint; compare 2 Kgs 9:30.

The skills match the names of the angels (see the note at 6:7). The Ethiopic list is shorter and corrupt (it has “Baraqiyal taught astrology, Kokabel the constellations, Ezeqeel the knowledge of the clouds”); this rendering follows the Greek more closely.

verses.text: Then Michael, Sariel,{a} Raphael, and Gabriel looked down from heaven and saw a great deal of blood being shed on the earth and all the lawlessness being done on the earth.
They said to one another, “The earth, stripped of its inhabitants,{b} raises the sound of their cry to the gates of heaven.
Now the souls of humankind are pleading with you, the holy ones of heaven: ‘Bring our case before the Most High.’”

They said to the Lord of the ages:{c} “You are Lord of lords, God of gods, King of kings, God of the ages! Your glorious throne stands for every generation of the ages, and your name is holy, glorious, and blessed for all the ages!
You made everything, and you have authority over everything. All things are bare and open before you; you see everything, and nothing can hide from you.
You see what Asael has done: he has taught all wrongdoing on the earth and revealed the eternal secrets that were kept in heaven, which human beings were striving to learn.{d}
And Shemihazah, to whom you gave authority to rule over those who are with him, has taught spells.
They have gone in to the daughters of men on the earth, lain with the women, defiled themselves, and revealed to them every kind of sin.
The women have borne giants,{e} and through this the whole earth has been filled with blood and wrongdoing.

And now, look: the souls of those who have died are crying out and making their appeal to the gates of heaven. Their groaning has gone up and cannot cease because of the lawless deeds done on the earth.
You know all things before they happen. You see these things and allow them, and you do not tell us what we ought to do to them about these things.”

notes.text: *Michael*: “Who is like God?” *Sariel*: “prince of God”; so the Greek and, reportedly, the Aramaic. The Ethiopic has *Uriel*, “God is my light.” *Raphael*: “God has healed.” *Gabriel*: “God is my strength” or “man of God.”
Stripped of its inhabitants: or “laid waste.” The Greek reads “The voice of their cry, as they are destroyed on the earth, reaches the gates of heaven.”
The Lord of the ages: so the Ethiopic; the Greek has “to the Lord, the King.”
Which human beings were striving to learn: so the Ethiopic; one Greek text reads “which the sons of men practice.”
Giants: the Greek of Syncellus adds “bastards.”

verses.text: Then the Most High, the Great Holy One, spoke. He sent Sariel{a} to the son of Lamech,{b}

saying, “Go to Noah{c} and tell him in my name, ‘Hide yourself!’ Reveal to him the end that is coming: that the whole earth will be destroyed, and a flood is about to come upon the whole earth and destroy everything on it.
Now teach him so that he may escape and his offspring may be preserved for all the generations of the world.”
To Raphael the Lord said, “Bind Asael hand and foot and throw him into the darkness. Make an opening in the desert that is in Dudael,{d} and throw him into it.
Lay rough and jagged rocks on him, cover him with darkness, and let him stay there forever. Cover his face so that he cannot see the light.
On the great day of judgment he will be thrown into the fire.

Heal the earth that the angels have ruined, and announce the healing of the earth, that I will heal the earth,{e} so that not all human beings will perish through all the secret things that the Watchers revealed and taught their sons.
The whole earth has been ruined by the teaching of the works of Asael; charge all sin to him.”

To Gabriel the Lord said, “Go against the bastards and the outcasts, the children of fornication. Destroy the children of the Watchers from among human beings. Send them against one another, so that they destroy each other in battle, for they will not have length of days.
No request that their fathers make of you for them will be granted, for they hope to live an everlasting life, and that each of them will live five hundred years.”
To Michael the Lord said, “Go, inform Shemihazah{f} and the others with him who have united themselves with women, so that they defiled themselves with them in all their uncleanness.

When their sons have killed one another and they have seen the destruction of their loved ones, bind them for seventy generations under the hills of the earth{g} until the day of their judgment and their end, until the judgment that is forever and ever is completed.
In those days they will be led away to the abyss of fire, to the torment, and to the prison where they will be shut up forever.
Whoever is condemned and destroyed will from then on be bound together with them until the end of all generations.
Wipe out every spirit of the outcasts{h} and of the Watchers’ children, for they have done wrong to the human race.

Rid the face of the earth of all wrongdoing; put an end to every evil deed, and let the plant of righteousness and truth come into view. It will become a blessing: deeds of righteousness and truth will be planted in truth and joy forever.

Then all the righteous will escape,
and they will live until they father thousands,
and all the days of their youth and their old age
they will complete in peace.
Then the whole earth will be farmed in righteousness; it will all be planted with trees and be full of blessing.

All pleasant trees will be planted on it, and they will plant vines on it. The vine that they plant on it will yield wine in abundance, and of all the seed that is sown on it each measure will yield a thousand, and each measure of olives will yield ten presses of oil.
Cleanse the earth from all oppression, from all wrongdoing, from all sin and godlessness; remove from the earth all the uncleanness that is done on it.
All human beings will become righteous, and all the nations will worship me and bless me, and all will bow down to me.
The earth will be cleansed from all defilement and from all sin, from all punishment and all torment, and I will never again send these upon it, from generation to generation and forever.

notes.text: *Sariel*: so the Greek (*Istraēl*, a corruption); the Ethiopic has *Arsyalalyur*, an unexplained name. See the note at 9:1.
*Lamech*: Hebrew *Lemekh*, meaning uncertain, perhaps “strong youth.” His son is Noah (Gen 5:28–29).
*Noah*: Hebrew *Noaḥ*, “rest,” linked in Gen 5:29 with *naḥam*, “to comfort.”
*Dudael*: perhaps “cauldron of God” or “jagged ground of God”; the place cannot be identified. Compare the wilderness of the scapegoat in Lev 16:10, 22.
That I will heal the earth: so the Greek; the Ethiopic reads “that they may heal the plague.”
Inform: so the Greek; the Ethiopic has “bind.”
Under the hills of the earth: so the Greek; the Ethiopic has “in the valleys of the earth.”
The outcasts: or “the lustful,” the giants; the word is uncertain.

verses.text: “In those days I will open the storehouses of blessing that are in heaven, to send them down upon the earth, upon the work and labor of human beings.
Truth and peace will be joined together through all the days of the world and through all the generations of humankind.”
Before these things Enoch was hidden,{a} and none of the human race knew where he was hidden, where he lived, or what had become of him.
He spent all his time with the Watchers, and his days were passed among the holy ones.{b}
While I, Enoch, stood blessing the great Lord, the King of the ages, the Watchers summoned me, Enoch the scribe, and told me,

“Enoch, scribe of righteousness, go and announce to the Watchers of heaven, who abandoned the high heaven and the holy, everlasting sanctuary, and have defiled themselves with women, and have done as human beings do, and have taken wives for themselves: ‘You have brought great destruction on the earth,
and you will have no peace or forgiveness of sin.’ Since they delight in their children,
they will see the slaughter of their loved ones and mourn over the destruction of their sons. They will plead forever, but they will obtain neither mercy nor peace.”

notes.text: Was hidden: or “was taken,” echoing Gen 5:24, “he was not, for God took him.”
The Watchers... the holy ones: here the faithful angels of heaven.

verses.text: Enoch went and said to Asael, “You will have no peace. A severe sentence has gone out against you, to bind you.
You will have no relief and no request granted, because of the wrongdoing that you taught and because of all the works of godlessness, wrongdoing, and sin that you showed to human beings.”
Then I went and spoke to all of them together, and they were all afraid; fear and trembling seized them.
They begged me to write a petition for them, so that they might find forgiveness, and to read their petition aloud in the presence of the Lord of heaven.
For from that time on they could not speak with him or lift up their eyes to heaven, out of shame for their sins for which they had been condemned.
So I wrote out their petition and the prayer concerning their spirits and their deeds one by one, and concerning their requests, that they might have forgiveness and length of days.
I went off and sat down by the waters of Dan,{a} in the land of Dan, to the southwest of Hermon, and I read their petition aloud until I fell asleep.
And look, a dream came to me, and visions fell upon me. I saw visions of punishment, and a voice came, telling me to speak to the sons of heaven and rebuke them.
When I woke up, I went to them. They were all sitting together weeping at Abel-main,{b} which is between Lebanon and Senir, with their faces covered.
I related to them every vision I had seen while asleep, and I began to speak words of righteousness and to rebuke the heavenly Watchers.

notes.text: *Dan*: “judge.” The waters of Dan are the springs of the Jordan at Tel Dan, at the foot of Mount Hermon.

*Abel-main*: “meadow of waters,” probably Abel-beth-maacah near Dan (2 Sam 20:14–15); the Ethiopic has *’Ubelseyāel* and the Greek *Ebelsata*, corruptions of the same name. *Senir*: the Amorite name of Hermon (Deut 3:9).

verses.text: This book is the word of righteousness and of the rebuke of the Watchers who are from eternity, according to the command of the Great Holy One in that vision.
In my sleep I saw what I now tell with a tongue of flesh and the breath of my mouth, which the Great One gave to humankind for speaking and for understanding in the heart.
As he created human beings and gave them the power to understand the word of knowledge, so he created me also and gave me the power to rebuke the Watchers, the sons of heaven.

I wrote out your petition, and in my vision it was shown to me that your petition will not be granted to you through all the days of eternity, and that judgment has been passed on you; your request will not be granted.
From now on you will not go up into heaven for all eternity. The decree has gone out to bind you in the earth for all the days of the world.
Before that, you will see the destruction of your beloved sons; you will have no pleasure in them, but they will fall before you by the sword.
Your plea for them will not be granted, nor your plea for yourselves, even if you weep and pray and recite every word of the document I wrote.

The vision was shown to me in this way. Look, in the vision clouds called me, and mist summoned me; the course of the stars and the lightning hurried me along and drove me on, and the winds in the vision made me fly, lifted me upward, and carried me into heaven.
I went in until I came near a wall built of hailstones{a} and surrounded by tongues of fire, and it began to frighten me.
I went into the tongues of fire and came near a great house built of hailstones. The walls of the house were like a mosaic floor of hailstones, and its floor was of snow.{b}
Its ceiling was like the path of the stars and the lightning, and among them were fiery cherubim,{c} and their sky was water.
Flaming fire surrounded the walls, and its doors blazed with fire.
I entered that house. It was hot as fire and cold as snow, and there was nothing of the pleasures of life in it. Fear covered me, and trembling took hold of me.
As I was shaking and trembling, I fell on my face. And I saw in the vision,
and look, there was a second house, greater than the first. Its whole doorway stood open before me, and it was built of tongues of fire.
In every respect it so surpassed the first in splendor, magnificence, and size that I cannot describe to you its splendor and its size.
Its floor was of fire; above it were lightning and the path of the stars, and its ceiling too was blazing fire.
I looked and saw in it a lofty throne. Its appearance was like frost,{d} and its wheels were like the shining sun, and there was the sound{e} of cherubim.
From beneath the throne came out rivers of blazing fire, so that I could not look at it.{f}
The Great Glory was seated on it. His robe was brighter than the sun and whiter than any snow.
None of the angels could enter that house or look at his face because of its majesty and glory, and no flesh could look at him.
Flaming fire encircled him, a great fire burned in front of him, and no one around him could come near him. Myriads upon myriads stood in his presence, yet he needed no counselor.{g}
The holiest ones who were near him did not leave by night or depart from him.
All this while I had lain face down, trembling. Then the Lord himself called me, speaking with his own mouth: “Come here, Enoch, and hear my word.”
One of the holy ones came to me and roused me; he made me get up and come to the door, and I bowed my face downward.

notes.text: Hailstones: so the Greek; the Ethiopic has “crystals.”
Its floor was of snow: so the Greek; the Ethiopic has “its foundation was of crystal.”
Cherubim: Hebrew plural of *kerub*, winged heavenly beings who guard God’s throne (Exod 25:18–22; Ezek 1; 10).
Frost: or “ice” (Greek *krystallinon*, “ice-like”).
The sound: so the Greek, reading *phōnē*, “voice”; the Ethiopic has “vision.”
Compare Dan 7:9–10; Ezek 1:26–28.
He needed no counselor: so the Greek, “every word of his is deed”; the Ethiopic reads “and he needs no holy counsel.”

verses.text: He answered and said to me, and I heard his voice, “Do not be afraid, Enoch, righteous man and scribe of righteousness. Come here and hear my voice.
Go and say to the Watchers of heaven who sent you to intercede for them: ‘You ought to intercede for human beings, not human beings for you.

Why have you left the high, holy, and eternal heaven, lain with women, defiled yourselves with the daughters of men, taken wives for yourselves, and acted like the children of earth, and fathered giants as your sons?

Though you were holy and spiritual, living eternal life, you defiled yourselves with the blood of women; you fathered children with the blood of flesh, and like human beings you longed for flesh and blood, as those who die and perish do.
That is why I gave them wives, so that they might make them pregnant and have children by them, so that nothing would be lacking to them on the earth.
But you were formerly spiritual, living eternal life, immortal for all the generations of the world.
Therefore I did not appoint wives for you, for the spiritual beings of heaven have their dwelling in heaven.
But now the giants, who were born from spirit and flesh, will be called evil spirits on the earth, and their dwelling will be on the earth.

Evil spirits have come out of their bodies, because they were created from above;{a} their beginning and first origin is from the holy Watchers. They will be evil spirits on the earth, and they will be called evil spirits.
The spirits of heaven have their dwelling in heaven, but the spirits of the earth, which were born on the earth, will have their dwelling on the earth.{b}
The spirits of the giants oppress, destroy, attack, wage war, and crush on the earth, and they cause sorrow. They eat no food, yet they hunger and thirst, and they cause offenses.{c}
These spirits will rise up against human beings and against women, because they came out from them.

notes.text: Because they were created from above: so the Greek; the Ethiopic reads “because they were born from men.”
Charles regarded this verse as an addition, since it repeats verses 7–8.
They hunger and thirst: so the Ethiopic. The Greek is obscure and is sometimes taken to mean that they do not hunger, but cause illnesses.

verses.text: “‘From the day of the slaughter and destruction and death of the giants, the spirits that have gone out from their bodies{a} will destroy without facing judgment. In this way they will destroy until the day of the completion, the great judgment, in which the great age will be completed upon the Watchers and the godless; it will be wholly completed.’
And now say to the Watchers who sent you to intercede for them, who were formerly in heaven,

‘You were in heaven, but not all the mysteries had been revealed to you. You knew a worthless mystery,{b} and in the hardness of your hearts you made it known to the women, and through this mystery women and men are doing much evil on the earth.’
So say to them, ‘You have no peace.’”

notes.text: From their bodies: literally “from the souls of their flesh.”
A worthless mystery: so the Greek; the Ethiopic has “rejected mysteries.”

verses.text: They took me and brought me to a place where those who were there looked like blazing fire, and whenever they wished, they took on the appearance of men.
They led me to the place of storm{a} and to a mountain whose highest peak reached into heaven.
I saw the places of the lights, the storehouses of the stars and of the thunder, and in the farthest depths a bow of fire, arrows with their quiver, a sword of fire, and all the lightning flashes.
They brought me to the waters of life,{b} and to the fire of the west, where the sun goes down each evening.
I came to a river of fire whose fire flows like water and pours out into the great sea in the west.
I viewed the great rivers; I reached the great river and the great darkness and went on to where no living creature walks.
I saw the mountains of the winter darkness and the place from which the water of every abyss pours out.
Every river on earth, I saw where it emptied, and where the abyss opens.

notes.text: Storm: so the Greek (*zophōdē*, “gloomy, stormy”); the Ethiopic has “darkness.”
The waters of life: literally “living waters,” that is, running water; here perhaps the waters at the edge of the world.

verses.text: I saw the storerooms of all the winds, and I saw how with them he has adorned the whole creation, and the foundations of the earth.
I saw the cornerstone of the earth. I saw the four winds that hold up the earth and the vault of the sky.
I saw how the winds spread out the height of heaven and stand between heaven and earth; they are the pillars of the sky.
I saw the winds of heaven that turn and lead the circle of the sun and all the stars to their setting.
I saw the earthly winds bearing the clouds along, and the roads the angels travel, and, at the earth’s edge, the sky’s vault overhead.
I went on toward the south{a} and saw a place burning day and night, where there were seven mountains of precious stones, three toward the east and three toward the south.
Of those toward the east, one was of colored stone, one of pearl, and one of healing stone;{b} those toward the south were of red stone.
The middle one reached to heaven like the throne of God; it was of antimony,{c} and the top of the throne was of sapphire.
I saw a blazing fire. Beyond these mountains
lies a region where the great earth stops and the heavens are finished.
I saw a great chasm among pillars of heavenly fire, and I saw in it pillars of fire falling, beyond measure both in height and in depth.
Beyond that chasm I saw a place that had no vault of heaven above it and no solid ground beneath it. There was no water on it and no birds; it was a desolate and dreadful place.
Seven stars were there, like huge mountains on fire. When I inquired about them,
the angel told me, “Here heaven and earth come to their limit. This place now serves as a jail for the stars and the heavenly host.
The stars that roll over the fire are those that disobeyed the command of the Lord at the beginning of their rising, because they did not come out at their proper times.
He was angry with them and bound them until the time when their sin is completed, for ten thousand years.”{d}

notes.text: Toward the south: so the Greek; the Ethiopic lacks the direction.
Healing stone: so the Greek (*iaseōs*); the Ethiopic has “jacinth” or “antimony.” The identification of these stones is uncertain.
Antimony: so the Ethiopic; the Greek has *phouka*, perhaps a dark stone. Compare the sapphire of the divine throne in Exod 24:10 and Ezek 1:26.
Ten thousand years: so the Greek; the Ethiopic has “in the year of the mystery.”

verses.text: Sariel{a} said to me, “Here will stand the angels who mixed with women. Their spirits, taking many forms, defile humankind and lead people astray into sacrificing to demons as to gods. Here they will stand until the day of the great judgment, when they will be judged until they are finished.
Their women, the wives of the angels who went astray, will become sirens.”{b}
I, Enoch, alone saw the sight, the ends of all things, and no human being will see what I have seen.

notes.text: *Sariel*: “prince of God”; so the Aramaic and Greek here, reportedly; the Ethiopic has *Uriel*. Compare 9:1.
Sirens: so the Greek (*seirēnas*); in the Greek Old Testament the word renders desert creatures (Isa 13:21). The Ethiopic reads “will become peaceful,” a misreading of the Greek.

verses.text: Here are the names of the holy angels who stand watch:
Uriel,{a} one of the holy angels, in charge of the world and of Tartarus.{b}
Raphael, a holy angel, in charge of human spirits.
Raguel, a holy angel, who brings punishment on the world of the lights.
Michael, a holy angel, placed in charge of the finest of humankind, the people.{c}
Saraqael, a holy angel, in charge of the spirits of those who sin in spirit.
Gabriel, a holy angel, in charge of Paradise, the serpents, and the cherubim.
Remiel, a holy angel, whom God put in charge of those who rise.{d}

notes.text: *Uriel*: “God is my light.” For the other names see the note at 9:1. *Raguel*: “friend of God.” *Saraqael* (Greek *Sariēl*): perhaps “God has struck” or “prince of God.” *Remiel*: “God has raised up” or “mercy of God.”
Tartarus: in Greek thought the deepest part of the underworld, where rebel powers are imprisoned; compare 2 Pet 2:4. The Ethiopic has “thunder and trembling.”
Over the people: so the Greek; the Ethiopic has “over chaos.” Michael is the guardian of Israel (Dan 10:21; 12:1).
Verse 8 is found only in one Greek copy, which also gives the total as seven archangels.

verses.text: I traveled on to where there was nothing made.{a}
There I saw something dreadful: I saw neither a heaven above nor solid ground below, but a desolate and fearful place.
In it seven heavenly stars lay tied together, burning, as large as great mountains.
Then I asked, “For what sin have they been bound, and why have they been thrown here?”
Uriel, a holy angel who accompanied me and who led them, replied, “Enoch, what is your question for, and why are you so eager for the truth?
These are some of the stars of heaven that disobeyed the command of the Lord. They have been bound here until ten thousand years are completed, the time required by their sins.”

From there I went to another place, more dreadful than the first. I saw a terrible thing there: a great fire burning and blazing. The place had a cleft reaching down to the abyss, full of great columns of fire falling downward. I could not see its size or its extent, nor could I estimate it.
Then I said, “How frightening this place is, and how terrible to look at!”
Uriel, one of the holy angels who was with me, answered, “Enoch, why are you so afraid and terrified?” I answered, “Because of this frightening place and this sight of pain.”
He said to me, “This place is the prison of the angels. They will be held here forever.”

notes.text: Where there was nothing made: or “to the place of chaos”; literally “to the formless.”

verses.text: Next I traveled to another place, where he pointed out to me in the west a great, high mountain and a hard rock.{a}

In it were four hollow places, deep and very smooth: three of them were dark and one was bright, with a spring of water in the middle of it.{b} I said, “How smooth these hollows are, how deep and dark to look at!”

Raphael, a holy angel who accompanied me, replied, “These hollows were made for exactly this: that the spirits of the souls of the dead might gather in them. They were made so that all the souls of human beings might gather here.
These places were made to hold them until the day of their judgment and until their appointed time, until the great judgment comes upon them.”
I saw the spirit of a dead man pleading, and its voice went out to heaven, making its case.{c}
I asked Raphael, the angel who was with me, “Whose spirit is this, whose voice goes up to heaven making its plea?”

He answered me, “This is the spirit that came out of Abel,{d} whom his brother Cain killed. He goes on accusing him until his offspring is destroyed from the face of the earth and his descendants have disappeared from the descendants of humankind.”
Then I asked about all the hollows: “Why is each one separated from the others?”
He answered me, “These three{e} were made to separate the spirits of the dead. This one has been set apart for the spirits of the righteous, where the bright spring of water is.
This one is for sinners who die and are laid in the ground without having been judged while they lived.

Here their spirits are kept apart in this great pain until the great day of judgment, of punishment, and of torment for those who curse forever, and of vengeance on their spirits. There he will bind them forever.
This one has been set apart for the spirits of those who make accusation, who disclose how they were destroyed, when they were murdered in the days of the sinners.

This one was made for the spirits of people who were not godly but sinners, complete in lawlessness, who will be companions of the lawless. Their spirits will not be punished on the day of judgment, nor will they be raised from here.”
Then I blessed the Lord of glory and said, “Blessed are you, Lord, the righteous Judge, who rules forever.”{f}

notes.text: A great, high mountain and a hard rock: so the Greek; the Ethiopic reads “a great and high mountain of hard rock.”
Three of them were dark... in the middle of it: so the Greek; the Ethiopic lacks these words. An Aramaic fragment (4QEnᵉ) is reported to read “deep and wide.”
So the Greek; the Ethiopic reads “I saw the spirits of the sons of men who were dead.”

*Abel*: Hebrew *Hevel*, “breath” or “vapor.” *Cain*: Hebrew *Qayin*, connected in Gen 4:1 with *qanah*, “to acquire.” Compare Gen 4:10, “Your brother’s blood cries out to me from the ground,” and Heb 12:24.
These three: some take this to mean “these”; four places are described in verses 9–13.
So the Greek, approximately; the Ethiopic reads “Blessed be my Lord, the Lord of righteousness, who rules forever.”

verses.text: From there I went to another place, to the west, at the ends of the earth.
I saw a fire blazing and running without rest; it did not stop its course day or night but kept on in the same way.
I asked, “What is this that never rests?”
Raguel, a holy angel who accompanied me, replied, “This running fire before you is the fire in the west that drives on all the lights of heaven.”
From there I went to another place on the earth, and he showed me a range of mountains of fire that burned day and night.

I went beyond it and saw seven splendid mountains, each different from the others. Their stones were precious and beautiful, the whole range splendid, glorious to look at and lovely in form: three toward the east, set firmly one on another, and three toward the south, one on another, with deep, winding ravines, none of which joined any other.
The seventh mountain stood in the middle of them and rose above them in height, like the seat of a throne, and fragrant trees surrounded the throne.

Among them was a tree whose like I had never smelled; neither among these nor among others was there one like it. It had a fragrance beyond every fragrance, and its leaves, its blossoms, and its wood never wither. Its fruit is beautiful and is like the clusters of a date palm.
Then I said, “What a beautiful tree this is, and how fragrant! Its leaves are lovely, and its blossoms are a delight to the eye.”
Then Michael, one of the holy and honored angels, who was with me and was their leader, answered me.
He said to me, “Enoch, why do you ask me about the fragrance of the tree, and why do you want to learn the truth?”
I replied, “I wish to understand all things, and this tree above all.”

He replied, “This lofty mountain before you, whose peak resembles God’s throne, really is his throne, where the Great Holy One, the Lord of glory, the King of eternity, will sit when he comes down to visit the earth with goodness.

As for this fragrant tree, no flesh has authority to touch it until the great judgment, when he will take vengeance on all and bring everything to its completion forever. Then it will be given to the righteous and the humble.
Its fruit will be food for the chosen. It will be moved to the holy place, to the house of the Lord, the King of eternity.{a}

Then they will rejoice greatly and be glad,
and they will enter the holy place.
Its fragrance will be in their bones,
and they will live a long life on the earth,
as your ancestors lived;
in their days no sorrow or pain,
no toil or affliction will touch them.”
Then I blessed the God of glory, the King of eternity, who has prepared such things for the righteous, has created them, and has promised to give them to them.

notes.text: Moved to the holy place: probably Jerusalem, described in chapter 26. The tree recalls the tree of life (Gen 2:9; 3:22; Rev 22:2, 14).

verses.text: From there I went to the center of the earth and saw a blessed place with trees whose branches were alive and sprouting from a tree that had been cut down.{a}
There I saw a holy mountain,{b} and beneath the mountain, to its east, there was water,{c} and it flowed toward the south.
I saw toward the east another mountain higher than this one, and between them a deep, narrow ravine; a stream ran through it, at the foot of the mountain.
To the west of it was another mountain, lower than it and not high, and between them a deep, dry ravine; and another deep, dry ravine lay at the far end of the three mountains.
All the ravines were deep and narrow, of hard rock, and no trees were planted in them.
I was amazed at the rock, and amazed at the ravine; I was very much amazed.

notes.text: The center of the earth: Jerusalem (compare Ezek 38:12; Jubilees 8:19). The cut tree that sprouts may allude to Israel’s restoration (compare Isa 11:1).

A holy mountain: Mount Zion. The mountain to the east is the Mount of Olives; the stream is the spring of Gihon and the Kidron; the lower mountain to the west is perhaps the Hill of Evil Counsel or the western hill; the deep ravines are the Kidron and Hinnom valleys.
Water: so the Greek; the Ethiopic has “a stream.”

verses.text: Then I said, “Why is this land blessed and wholly filled with trees, while this ravine between is cursed?”

Then Sariel,{a} one of the holy angels who was with me, answered, “This cursed valley is for those who are cursed forever. Here all those will be gathered who speak improper words against the Lord with their mouths and say harsh things about his glory. Here they will be gathered, and here will be their place of judgment.{b}

In the last days there will be the spectacle of a righteous judgment upon them in the presence of the righteous forever. Here those who have found mercy will bless the Lord of glory, the King of eternity.
In the days of their judgment{c} they will bless him for the mercy he has shown them, for he has assigned them their lot.”
Then I blessed the Lord of glory; I proclaimed his glory and praised him as befits his majesty.

notes.text: *Sariel*: so the Greek; the Ethiopic has *Uriel*. See the notes at 9:1 and 19:1.
This cursed valley: the Valley of Hinnom (Gehenna), south of Jerusalem, a place of child sacrifice under the kings (Jer 7:31–32) and later an image of final punishment (Isa 66:24; Mark 9:43–48).
Their judgment: the judgment of the wicked.

verses.text: From there I went eastward into the middle of the mountain range of the wilderness, and I saw desert land, lonely, but full of trees and plants.{a}
Water gushed out from above.
It streamed like an abundant watercourse flowing toward the northwest, and from every side it sent up water and dew.{b}

notes.text: But full of trees and plants: so the Greek; the Ethiopic places the trees after the water of verse 2.
Water and dew: so the Greek; the Ethiopic has “clouds and dew.”

verses.text: From there I went to another place in the wilderness, to the east of this mountain range, and came near it.
There I saw trees of judgment,{a} breathing out the fragrance of frankincense and myrrh, and the trees were not like ordinary trees.{b}

notes.text: Trees of judgment: so the Ethiopic, perhaps a corruption; the Greek has “aromatic trees.”
Not like ordinary trees: so the Greek, approximately; the Ethiopic has “similar to the almond tree.”

verses.text: Past these I journeyed a long way east and came upon another place, a well-watered valley,
with a tree in it the color of fragrant trees, like the mastic.{a}
Fragrant cinnamon grew along the valley slopes. Past them I continued east.

notes.text: Mastic: an aromatic resin from the mastic tree (*Pistacia lentiscus*). The Greek here is uncertain.

verses.text: I saw other mountains, and on them were trees from which flowed nectar called *sarara* and galbanum.{a}
Beyond these mountains I saw another mountain, and on it were aloe trees,{b} all full of stacte, like almond trees.
When one burns it, it smells sweeter than any perfume.

notes.text: *Sarara*: an aromatic not otherwise known, perhaps storax. Galbanum is a fragrant gum resin used in the incense of the tabernacle (Exod 30:34).
Aloe trees: aloeswood, a fragrant wood; compare Ps 45:8; Prov 7:17. *Stacte*: a fragrant resin (Exod 30:34), perhaps from storax or myrrh.

verses.text: Leaving these fragrances behind, as I gazed northward{a} over the mountains, I saw seven mountains full of choice nard, fragrant trees, cinnamon, and pepper.
From there I passed over the summits of all those mountains, far to the east of the earth. I crossed above the Red Sea{b} and went far beyond it, and I passed over the darkness,{c} far from it.

I came to the Garden of Righteousness. From far off I saw trees more numerous and greater than these, of fine fragrance, very beautiful and glorious, and the tree of wisdom, whose fruit the holy ones eat and gain great wisdom.
That tree is as tall as a fir; its leaves are like those of the carob, and its fruit is like a cluster of grapes, very beautiful. Its fragrance spreads far beyond the tree.
Then I said, “How beautiful this tree is, and how pleasing to look at!”

Raphael, the holy angel accompanying me, replied, “That is the tree of wisdom. Your father and mother of old, who lived long before you, ate from it; they gained wisdom, their eyes were opened, they realized they were naked, and they were expelled from the garden.”{d}

notes.text: Toward the north: the Greek has “toward the northeast.”
The Red Sea: so the Greek (*Erythra thalassa*), which in ancient usage included the Indian Ocean and the Persian Gulf.
The darkness: so the Greek (*zotiēl* is read as a corruption of *zophos*, “darkness”); the Ethiopic reads “the angel Zotiel.”

Your aged father and your aged mother: Adam and Eve. *Adam*: Hebrew *’adam*, “human being,” connected with *’adamah*, “ground” (Gen 2:7). *Eve*: Hebrew *Ḥawwah*, connected with *ḥay*, “living” (Gen 3:20). Compare Gen 3:6–7, 23–24.

verses.text: From there I went to the ends of the earth and saw great animals there, each different from the others, and also birds different in appearance, beauty, and voice, each from the other.
East of those animals I saw the ends of the earth on which heaven rests, and the gates of heaven open.

I watched the heavenly stars emerge; I counted the gates they emerge from and recorded every exit, star by star: how many, what each is called, its route, its station, its seasons, and its months, just as Uriel, the holy angel at my side, pointed them out.
He showed me everything and wrote it down for me. He also wrote down their names for me, and their laws and their functions.
Then I traveled north to the earth’s farthest reaches, and at the edge of the whole world I beheld a great and splendid marvel.
Three heavenly gates stood open in the sky there, and north winds issue from each; their blowing brings cold and hail, frost and snow, dew and rain.
Through one gate they blow to bring benefit; through the other two they blow violently and bring hardship on the earth.
From there I went westward to the ends of the earth, and there I saw three gates of heaven open, just as I had seen in the east: the same number of gates and the same number of exits.
From there I went southward to the ends of the earth, and there I saw three open gates of heaven, from which come dew, rain, and wind.
From there I went eastward to the ends of heaven, and there I saw the three eastern gates of heaven open, with small gates above them.
Through each of these small gates the stars of heaven pass and run their course westward on the path that has been shown to them.

Each time I saw these things I praised the Lord of glory, and I keep praising the Lord of glory, who has worked great and glorious wonders so that angels, spirits, and mortals may behold how great his work is, may praise what he has made and all his creatures, may witness what his power does, may extol the mighty work of his hands, and may bless him forever.
The second vision that he saw, a vision of wisdom, which Enoch saw, son of Jared, son of Mahalalel, son of Kenan, son of Enosh, son of Seth, son of Adam.{a}

This is how the words of wisdom begin, which I raised my voice to speak and declare to those who live on the dry ground: Listen, you people of former times, and look, you who come later, at the words of the Holy One that I will speak before the Lord of Spirits.{b}
It would have been fitting to tell these things to the ancients alone, but we will not keep the beginning of wisdom back from those who come after either.
Never until now has the Lord of Spirits granted such wisdom as I have received, in keeping with my understanding and by the will of the Lord of Spirits, who has given me a share in everlasting life.
Three discourses{c} were given to me, and I raised my voice and told them to those who live on the dry ground.

notes.text: *Mahalalel*: “praise of God.” *Kenan* (Ethiopic *Qāynān*): perhaps “smith” or “possession.” *Enosh*: “human being, mortal.” *Seth*: “appointed” or “granted” (Gen 4:25). The genealogy follows Gen 5:3–18. “The second vision” counts the Book of the Watchers (chapters 1–36) as the first. This section, called “the Parables” or “Similitudes,” survives only in Ge'ez; no Aramaic or Greek fragment of it has been found. Its date is debated, with most recent scholars placing it in the late first century BC or the first century AD.

The Lord of Spirits: the standard title for God in chapters 37–71, used over a hundred times; compare “the God of the spirits of all flesh” in Num 16:22; 27:16, and “Yahweh of hosts” in the Hebrew Bible, which it may echo.
Discourses: Ge'ez *mesālē*, like Hebrew *mashal*, “parable, proverb, figurative speech, oracle” (compare Num 23:7). The three are chapters 38–44, 45–57, and 58–69.

verses.text:
The first discourse.
When the community of the righteous appears,
and sinners are judged for their sins
and driven from the face of the dry ground;

when the Righteous One{a} appears in the sight of the righteous,
whose chosen deeds depend on the Lord of Spirits,
and light shines on the righteous and the chosen who live on the dry ground—
where then will the sinners live,
and where will those who denied the Lord of Spirits find rest?
It would have been better for them never to have been born.{b}

When the secrets of the righteous are disclosed,
the sinners are judged,
and the wicked are driven out from the presence of the righteous and the chosen,

from then on those who hold the land will no longer be mighty and lofty;
they will not be able to look at the face of the holy ones,
for the Lord of Spirits will have made his light appear
on the faces of the holy, the righteous, and the chosen.

Then the kings and the powerful will perish,
handed over to the righteous and the holy.

From then on no one will plead for mercy for them from the Lord of Spirits,
for their life will be over.

notes.text: The Righteous One: one of four titles in the Parables for the heavenly figure who judges at the end: “the Righteous One,” “the Chosen One,” “the Anointed One” (48:10; 52:4), and “that Son of Man.” Some manuscripts read “righteousness” here.
Compare Matt 26:24; Mark 14:21.

verses.text: In those days chosen and holy children will come down from the high heaven, and their offspring will be joined with the children of humankind.{a}

In those days Enoch received books of jealous anger and fury, books of turmoil and banishment.
“No mercy will be granted to them,” says the Lord of Spirits.

In those days a whirlwind{b} snatched me up from the earth
and put me down at the far end of the heavens.

There I saw another vision:
the homes of the holy ones
and the resting places of the righteous.

There my eyes beheld their homes among his righteous angels,
their resting places among the holy ones.
They were petitioning, pleading, and praying for the children of humankind;
righteousness flowed before them like water,
and mercy like dew on the ground.
So it is among them forever and ever.

In those days{c} my eyes saw the Chosen One of righteousness and faithfulness.
Righteousness will prevail in his days,
and the righteous and chosen will be beyond number before him forever and ever.

I saw his home under the wings of the Lord of Spirits.
All the righteous and chosen before him will shine like flames of fire;
their mouths will be full of blessing,
their lips will praise the name of the Lord of Spirits,
and righteousness will never fail before him,
nor will truth fail in his presence.

There I longed to live;
my spirit yearned for that home.
That is where my share has been from the start,
for so it was settled for me before the Lord of Spirits.
In those days I praised and exalted the name of the Lord of Spirits with blessing and praise, for he has destined me for blessing and glory by the good pleasure of the Lord of Spirits.
For a long time my eyes gazed at that place, and I gave him blessing and praise: “Blessed be he! From the beginning and for all time to come may he be blessed!
In his presence nothing ends. He knew before the world was made what the age is and what will be from generation to generation.
There my eyes saw all who never sleep, standing before him and blessing him and saying, “Blessed are you, and blessed is the name of the Lord forever and ever.”
My face was transformed, for I could no longer bear to look.

notes.text: Verses 1–2a seem to refer back to the Watchers (chapters 6–16), and some take them as an insertion.
A whirlwind: or “a cloud and a storm.” Compare Elijah in 2 Kgs 2:11.
In those days: Charles transposes parts of verses 6 and 7; this translation keeps the order of the manuscripts.
Compare Isa 6:3, “Holy, holy, holy is Yahweh of hosts; the whole earth is full of his glory.” “Those who never sleep” are the Watchers (compare 14:23).

verses.text: After that I saw thousands upon thousands and myriads upon myriads, a throng past all counting and reckoning, standing before the Lord of Spirits.{a}

Around the Lord of Spirits, one on each of his four sides, stood four figures,{b} different from those who do not sleep, and I learned their names, since the angel accompanying me told me what they were called and showed me every hidden thing.
I heard the voices of those four figures as they spoke praises before the Lord of glory.
The first voice was blessing the Lord of Spirits forever and ever.
The second voice I heard blessing the Chosen One and the chosen ones who depend on the Lord of Spirits.
The third voice I heard praying and pleading for those who live on the dry ground and who call on the name of the Lord of Spirits.
The fourth voice I heard driving away the satans{c} and barring them from approaching the Lord of Spirits with accusations against those who live on the dry ground.
Then I put a question to the angel of peace, my companion, who had and showed me everything hidden, “Who are these four figures whom I have seen, whose words I have heard and written down?”

He told me, “The first is Michael, merciful and slow to anger. The second, who is set over every disease and every wound of humankind, is Raphael. The third, who is set over every power, is Gabriel. And the fourth, who is set over repentance and the hope of those who will inherit everlasting life, is named Phanuel.”{d}
Those were the Lord of Spirits’ four angels, and theirs were the four voices I heard in those days.

notes.text: Compare Dan 7:10.
Figures: literally “faces” or “presences,” the angels of the presence (compare Isa 63:9).
Satans: “accusers, adversaries” (Hebrew *satan*), here a class of hostile angels who accuse human beings before God; compare Job 1:6–12; Zech 3:1; Rev 12:10.

*Michael*: “Who is like God?” *Raphael*: “God heals.” *Gabriel*: “God is my strength” or “man of God.” *Phanuel*: “face of God” (compare Penuel, Gen 32:30). Phanuel takes the place of Uriel in the list of four at 9:1.

verses.text: After that I saw all the secrets of heaven, how the kingdom is divided up, and how human deeds are weighed on the scales.

There I saw the homes of the chosen and the homes of the holy ones. My eyes saw there all the sinners who deny the name of the Lord of Spirits being driven out and dragged away; they could not stay, because of the punishment that goes out from the Lord of Spirits.

There my eyes saw the secrets of the lightning and the thunder, the secrets of the winds, how they are portioned out to blow across the land, and what is hidden in cloud and dew. I saw there where they come from in that place, and from where they soak the dusty ground.

There I saw sealed storerooms from which the winds are portioned out: the storeroom of the hail, the storeroom of the mist, and the storeroom of the clouds, whose cloud has hovered over the earth since the world began.

I saw the chambers of the sun and the moon, from where they come out and where they return, their glorious going back, how one outranks the other, their majestic circuit, how they never leave their track, neither adding to it nor taking from it, and how they keep faith with each other by the oath that binds them.
First the sun goes out and travels its road at the command of the Lord of Spirits, whose name is mighty forever and ever.

Next I saw the moon’s path, both its hidden and its visible part. She completes the course of her path there by day and by night, each facing the other before the Lord of Spirits.
They give thanks and praise and never rest,
for their thanksgiving is their rest.

For the bright sun makes many turnings, for blessing or for curse,
and the course of the moon’s path
brings light for the righteous
and darkness for sinners, by the name of the Lord,
who separated light from darkness,
divided the spirits of humankind,
and strengthened the spirits of the just
through his righteous name.
No angel can stand in the way, nor can any power prevent it; he appoints one to judge them all, and that judge tries them all in his presence.

Wisdom found no place to live,
so a home was given her in the heavens.

Then Wrongdoing came out of her storerooms;
she found those she was not looking for,
and she lived among them,
like rain in a desert,
like dew on a thirsty land.

notes.text: Compare Prov 1:20–33; 8; Sir 24:1–12, where Wisdom finds a home in Israel; and John 1:10–11.

verses.text: Then I saw more lightning and the heavenly stars; he summoned each of them by name, and they listened to him.

I saw how they are weighed on a just scale according to their brightness: the breadth of their spaces and the day they appear, how their circling produces lightning, how their circling matches the number of the angels, and how they stay loyal to each other.
I asked the angel who went with me and showed me what was hidden, “What are these?”

He said to me, “The Lord of Spirits has shown you their meaning in a figure: these are the names of the holy ones who live on the dry ground and believe in the name of the Lord of Spirits forever and ever.”
I saw another thing concerning the lightning: how some of the stars rise and become lightning flashes and cannot give up their new form.
This is the second discourse, concerning those who reject the name of the holy ones’ dwelling and of the Lord of Spirits.

They will not go up into heaven,
nor will they come back upon the earth.
That is the fate awaiting sinners
who rejected the Lord of Spirits’ name,
held in this state for the day of suffering and distress.

For I have looked after my righteous ones and satisfied them with peace,
and placed them before me;
but for the sinners judgment waits with me,
to wipe them from the face of the earth.

notes.text: Choose among their deeds: or “test their deeds.”
Compare Isa 65:17; 66:22; 2 Pet 3:13; Rev 21:1.

verses.text:
There I beheld one with a head of days,{a}
his head as white as wool,
and beside him a second, whose face had a human look,
and his face was full of grace, like one of the holy angels.
I questioned the angel accompanying me, who was revealing every secret to me, about that Son of Man:{b} who he was, where he came from, and why he was accompanying the Head of Days.

This Son of Man whom you have seen
will rouse the kings and the powerful from their couches
and the strong from their thrones;
he will slacken the grip of the strong
and smash the teeth of sinners.

He will throw the kings down from their thrones and their kingdoms,
because they do not exalt and praise him
or humbly acknowledge where their kingship came from.

He will make the faces of the strong fall,
and shame will fill them.
Darkness will be their home,
and worms their bed;
they will have no hope of getting up from those beds,
since they refuse to exalt the name of the Lord of Spirits.

They hound the houses where his people gather
and the faithful who rely on the name of the Lord of Spirits.

notes.text: A head of days: that is, one who is very old; God, called “the Ancient of Days” in Dan 7:9, 13, 22. This chapter draws on Dan 7:9–14.

That Son of Man: in Ge'ez *walda sab'*; elsewhere in the Parables also *walda be'si* and *walda 'egwala 'emma-ḥeyāw*, all meaning “son of a human being,” that is, “a human figure,” as in Dan 7:13. The demonstrative (“that,” “this”) points back to the figure first seen here. Compare the Gospels’ use of “the Son of Man.”
Judge the stars of heaven: perhaps “attack the stars,” that is, the holy ones; compare Dan 8:10. Some propose “raise their hands against the stars.”
Their deeds are wrongdoing: so some manuscripts; others read “their power rests on their wealth.”

verses.text:
In those days the prayer of the righteous will have gone up,
and the righteous blood from the ground, into the presence of the Lord of Spirits.

In those days the holy ones who live in the heavens above
will join with one voice
to plead and pray, praise, give thanks, and bless the Lord of Spirits’ name
because of the blood of the righteous that has been shed,
that the righteous may not have prayed in vain before the Lord of Spirits,
that justice may be done for them,
and that their waiting may not go on forever.{a}

The hearts of the holy ones were filled with joy,
for the full number of the just had drawn near,{c}
the prayer of the just had been answered,
and the blood of the just had been avenged before the Lord of Spirits.

notes.text: Compare Rev 6:9–11.
Compare Dan 7:9–10; Rev 20:12.
Had drawn near: or “had been reached” or “had been offered.” Compare Rev 6:11.

verses.text:
In that place I saw the spring of righteousness,
which never ran dry,
and around it were many springs of wisdom.
All the thirsty drank from them
and were filled with wisdom,
and their homes were with the righteous, the holy, and the chosen.

At that hour that Son of Man was given his name
before the Lord of Spirits,
his name spoken in the Head of Days’ presence.

All who live on the dry ground will fall down and worship before him,
and will praise, bless, and sing to the Lord of Spirits.

For this reason he was chosen and hidden in his presence
before the world was created, and forever.

“I will hand them over to my chosen ones;
like straw in a fire they will burn before the holy,
like lead in water they will sink before the righteous,
and no trace of them will ever be found.

On the day of their distress there will be rest on the earth.
They will fall before him and not get up again,
and there will be no one to take them by the hand and lift them,
for they rejected the Lord of Spirits and his Anointed One.”{d}
Blessed be the Lord of Spirits’ name!

notes.text: Compare Ps 72:17, “May his name endure before the sun” (so the Greek and some Jewish interpretation).
He is the one who will avenge their lives: or “it is his will regarding their life.”
His Anointed One: Ge'ez *masiḥ*, “anointed,” the word behind “Messiah” (Hebrew *mashiaḥ*) and “Christ” (Greek *christos*). Compare Ps 2:2. Here and at 52:4 the title is applied to the Son of Man.

verses.text:
For wisdom is poured out like water,
and glory will never fail before him, forever and ever.

In him lives the spirit of wisdom,
the spirit that gives understanding,
the spirit of knowledge and power,
and the spirit of those who died in righteousness and sleep.{a}

notes.text: Compare Isa 11:2.

verses.text:
In those days a change will come for the holy and the chosen:
the light of days will rest on them,
and glory and honor will return to the holy ones

on the day of distress, when evil has been stored up against the sinners.
The righteous will triumph in the name of the Lord of Spirits,
and he will let the others see it,
so that they may repent
and abandon the works of their hands.

Before the Lord of Spirits they will receive no honor,
yet by his name they will find salvation,
and the Lord of Spirits will pity them,
for his mercy is great.{a}
“From then on I will show them no mercy,” says the Lord of Spirits.

notes.text: Verses 2–3 envision a third group, “the others,” who repent at the last moment and are saved without honor.

verses.text:
He will pick out the righteous and holy from among them,
for the day of their salvation has come near.{b}

For in those days the Chosen One will arise,
and the earth will rejoice;
the righteous will live on it,
and the chosen will go to and fro on it.

notes.text: Sheol: the Hebrew name for the realm of the dead. “Destruction” renders Ge'ez *haguel*, perhaps standing for Hebrew *Abaddon* (Job 26:6; Rev 9:11). The verse speaks of the resurrection of the dead; compare Dan 12:2; Rev 20:13.
Verses 2 and 5a are given here in the manuscript order; Charles moves the line “For in those days the Chosen One will arise” to the start of verse 2.
My throne: so most manuscripts; some read “his throne.” God is the speaker.
Compare Ps 114:4, 6.

verses.text: After those days, in the place where I had seen every vision of what is hidden—for a whirlwind had snatched me up and carried me westward—

my eyes saw there all the hidden things of heaven that are to come: a mountain of iron, a mountain of copper, a mountain of silver, a mountain of gold, a mountain of soft metal, and a mountain of lead.{a}
I asked the angel who went with me, “What are these hidden things I have seen?”
He told me, “Everything you have seen will serve the authority of his Anointed One, so that he may be strong and powerful on the earth.”
That angel of peace replied, “Wait a little, and you will be shown every hidden thing that surrounds the Lord of Spirits.

These mountains your eyes have seen—
of iron and of copper and of silver,
of gold, of soft metal, and of lead—
all of them will be before the Chosen One
like wax before fire,
like water pouring down from above onto those mountains;
they will grow weak under his feet.{b}

In those days no one will be saved
by gold or by silver,
and no one will be able to flee.

There will be no iron for battle,
no armor to put on;
bronze will be of no use,
tin will be worthless,
and lead will not be wanted.

All these will be wiped out from the face of the earth
when the Chosen One appears before the Lord of Spirits.”

notes.text: Soft metal: probably tin. The six mountains of metal may echo the metals of the statue in Dan 2:31–45, representing earthly empires and their wealth.
Compare Mic 1:4; Ps 97:5.

verses.text: There my eyes saw a deep valley with gaping mouths. All who live on the land, the sea, and the islands will bring it gifts, presents, and tribute, but that deep valley will never be filled.
For I saw all the angels of punishment staying there, getting ready all the instruments of Satan.{b}
I asked the angel of peace who went with me, “For whom are they getting these instruments ready?”
He told me, “They are preparing them for the kings and the powerful of this earth, so that they may be destroyed by them.
After this the Righteous and Chosen One will make the house of his congregation appear. From then on they will no longer be hindered, in the name of the Lord of Spirits.

notes.text: Whatever the righteous toil for: so some manuscripts; others read “the sinners devour all whom they oppress.”
Satan: here a single chief adversary; compare the plural “satans” at 40:7.
Will not stand firm like the earth: the sense is uncertain; perhaps “will be like level ground.”

verses.text: I looked and turned toward another part of the earth, and there I saw a deep valley burning with fire.
They were bringing the kings and the powerful and throwing them into that deep valley.
There my eyes watched them forging tools for it: chains of iron too heavy to weigh.
I asked my companion, the angel of peace, “Who are these chains being readied for?”

He told me, “They are being prepared for the armies of Azazel,{a} so that they may seize them and hurl them into the lowest part of the pit of damnation, and cover their jaws with jagged stones, as the Lord of Spirits has ordered.

Michael, Gabriel, Raphael, and Phanuel will grab hold of them on that great day and throw them into the blazing furnace on that day, so that the Lord of Spirits may punish them for their wickedness, because they became servants of Satan and misled those who live on the dry ground.”
In those days{b} punishment will go out from the Lord of Spirits. He will open all the storerooms of the waters above the heavens and the springs beneath the earth.{c}
All the waters will join together: the water above the heavens is the male, and the water beneath the earth is the female.
They will wipe out all who live on the dry ground and those who live under the ends of heaven.
Because of this they will come to recognize the wickedness they have done on the earth, and through these waters they will perish.

notes.text: *Azazel*: the Ethiopic form of the Aramaic *Asael*; see the note at 8:1. Compare Lev 16:8–10, 26.
Verses 54:7–55:2 seem to belong to a separate “Book of Noah” tradition; compare 60:1–10, 24–25; 65–69:25; 106–107. They describe the first world judgment, the flood.
Compare Gen 7:11.

verses.text: After that the Head of Days relented and said, “I have destroyed all who live on the dry ground for nothing.”

He swore by his great name: “From now on I will not act this way toward all who live on the dry ground. I will put a sign in the sky, and it will be a pledge of good faith between me and them forever, as long as heaven stands above the earth.{a} This is in keeping with my command.
When I decide to seize them through the angels on the day of distress and pain, I will make my punishment and my anger rest on them,” says God, the Lord of Spirits.

“You powerful kings who live on the dry ground, you will have to watch my Chosen One sit on the throne of glory and judge Azazel and all his companions and all his armies in the name of the Lord of Spirits.”

notes.text: A sign in the sky: the rainbow (Gen 9:8–17). Compare Gen 8:21–22.

verses.text: There I saw troops of the angels of punishment marching, holding whips and chains of iron and bronze.
I asked my companion, the angel of peace, “Where are these whip-bearers headed?”
He told me, “Each to its own chosen and beloved ones,{a} so that they may be flung into the chasm, the depths of the valley.

They will march up and trample the land of his chosen ones,
and the land of his chosen ones will be before them like a threshing floor and a beaten path.

In those days Sheol will open its jaws,
and they will sink into it;
their destruction will be complete.
Sheol will swallow the sinners in the presence of the chosen.”

notes.text: Its own chosen and beloved ones: that is, the favorites of the fallen angels, the giants (compare 10:12; 14:6).

The Parthians and Medes: the Parthian empire, east of the Euphrates, which invaded Syria and Judea in 40 BC. Many date the Parables partly by this allusion. *Medes*: the ancient people of Media, in northwest Iran.
The city of my righteous ones: Jerusalem. Compare Ezek 38–39; Zech 14:2–3, 13.

verses.text: After this I saw another army, of wagons with men riding on them, coming on the winds from the east and from the west toward the south.{a}

The rumble of their wagons was heard, and when that uproar happened, the holy ones in heaven took notice, and the pillars of the earth were shaken from their places. The noise of it was heard from one end of heaven to the other for one day.
Every one of them will bow low in worship before the Lord of Spirits. This is the end of the second discourse.

notes.text: This verse is often read as the return of the scattered Jews of the diaspora to Jerusalem; compare Isa 43:5–6; 49:22; 66:20.

verses.text: I began to speak the third discourse, about the righteous and the chosen.

How happy you will be, righteous and chosen ones,
for your lot will be glorious!

The righteous will live in the sunlight,
and the chosen in the light of everlasting life.
There will be no end to the days of their life,
and no counting the days of the holy ones.

They will seek the light and find righteousness with the Lord of Spirits.
Peace will belong to the righteous in the name of the Lord of the ages.

There will be unending light,
and they will never come to an end of days,
for the darkness will first have been destroyed,
and the light of uprightness will stand firm forever before the Lord of Spirits.
In those days my eyes saw the secrets of the lightning and the lights and the judgments they carry out. They flash for blessing or for curse, as the Lord of Spirits wills.

There I saw the secrets of the thunder: how, when it crashes in the heights of heaven, its sound is heard. He let me see the judgments carried out on the earth, whether for well-being and blessing or for curse, according to the word of the Lord of Spirits.
After that all the secrets of the lights and of the lightning were shown to me: they flash for blessing and for plenty.

In Enoch’s life, year five hundred, month seven, day fourteen.{a} In that discourse I saw how a violent shaking shook the heaven of heavens, and the host of the Most High, the angels, thousands upon thousands and myriads upon myriads, were greatly disturbed.
The Head of Days was sitting on the throne of his glory, with the angels and the righteous standing around him.

Great trembling seized me,
terror took hold of me;
my waist gave way,
my insides dissolved,
and I fell on my face.

Michael sent another angel, one of the holy ones, and he lifted me up. When he had lifted me up, my spirit came back to me, for I had not been able to bear the sight of that host, the uproar, and the shaking of heaven.
Michael said to me, “Why does a sight like this disturb you? Until today the day of his mercy has lasted; he has been merciful and slow to anger toward those who live on the dry ground.

But when the day comes, with the power, the punishment, and the judgment that the Lord of Spirits has made ready for those who do not bow to the just law, for those who deny the just judgment, and for those who take his name in vain—that day has been made ready: for the chosen a covenant, but for sinners an investigation.”
On that day two monsters will be separated from each other: a female monster named Leviathan,{b} to live in the depths of the sea above the springs of the waters,

and the male named Behemoth, who fills with his chest a trackless wilderness named Dendayin,{c} east of the garden where the chosen and righteous live, where my grandfather was received up,{d} he who was seventh from Adam, the first human being whom the Lord of Spirits created.
I asked the other angel to show me the strength of those monsters, how they were separated on one day and thrown, one into the depths of the sea and the other onto the dry ground of the wilderness.
He said to me, “You, son of man,{e} are seeking to know what is hidden.”

The other angel, who went with me and showed me hidden things, told me what is first and last in heaven, in the height, and beneath the dry ground, in the depth, and at the ends of heaven and at the foundations of heaven,

and about the storerooms of the winds: how the winds are divided up, how they are weighed, and how the gates of the winds are counted, each by the strength of its wind; the strength of the moon’s light, and how its strength is suited; the divisions of the stars by their names, and how every division is marked off;
the thunderclaps, by the places where they fall; all the divisions made among the lightning flashes so that they may flash; and their host, so that they obey at once.

The thunder has resting places, assigned to it while it waits for its crash. Thunder and lightning cannot be parted; though they are not one and the same, they travel together through the wind and do not separate.

For when the lightning flashes, the thunder sounds its voice, and the wind gives it rest at the right moment, dividing evenly between them. The storehouse of their crashes is like sand; each of them, as it crashes, is held back with a bridle, turned back by the power of the wind, and driven on to the many regions of the earth.
The wind of the sea is male and strong. By the might of its strength it reins the sea back, and in the same way it drives it forward and scatters it among all the mountains of the earth.
The wind of the frost is its own angel, and the wind of the hail is a good angel.
