The wind of the snow has left its storerooms because of its strength. There is a special wind in it, and what rises from it is like smoke; its name is hoarfrost.
The wind of the mist does not share their storerooms; it has a storeroom of its own, for its course is glorious in light and in darkness, in winter and in summer, and an angel is in its storeroom.

The wind of the dew lives at the ends of heaven and is joined to the storerooms of the rain. Its course is in winter and in summer, and its clouds and the clouds of the mist are joined; one gives to the other.

When the wind of the rain goes out of its storeroom, the angels come, open the storeroom, and lead it out. When it spreads over the whole dry ground, it unites with the water on the earth; and whenever it unites with the water on the earth . . .{f}
For the waters are for those who live on the dry ground; they are nourishment for the earth from the Most High in heaven. So there is a fixed measure for the rain, and the angels are in charge of it.
All this I saw near the Garden of the Righteous.
The angel of peace who was with me said to me, “These two monsters, prepared in keeping with the greatness of the Lord, will feed . . .{g}

so that the punishment of the Lord of Spirits may not come upon them for nothing. Children will be killed with their mothers, and children with their fathers. When the punishment of the Lord of Spirits rests on them, it will stay on them, so that the punishment of the Lord of Spirits may not be in vain. After that the judgment will take place in keeping with his mercy and his patience.”{h}

notes.text: In the life of Enoch: the date originally belonged to Noah (compare Gen 7:6, 11, where Noah is 600 at the flood); the editor who placed this Noah fragment here changed the name, but verse 8 still has Noah speaking of “my grandfather.” *The seventh month*: in the Jewish calendar Tishri, roughly September–October, the month of the Day of Atonement and Tabernacles; on the 364-day calendar of 1 Enoch and Jubilees, see the notes at chapter 72.
*Leviathan*: Hebrew *liwyatan*, perhaps “coiled one,” the sea monster of Job 41; Ps 74:14; 104:26; Isa 27:1. *Behemoth*: Hebrew plural of *behemah*, “beast,” meaning “the great beast” (Job 40:15–24).
*Dendayin*: the manuscripts vary (*Dendāin*, *Dâidâin*, *Dûidâin*). Perhaps a form of the desert “Dudael” (10:4), or of Nod “east of Eden” (Gen 4:16).
My grandfather: Enoch, grandfather of Noah's father Lamech; so the speaker here is Noah (see the note at verse 1). Enoch was “the seventh from Adam” (Gen 5:3–24; Jude 14).
Son of man: here simply “human being, mortal,” as in Ezekiel (Ezek 2:1).
The text is broken off here in all manuscripts.
Will feed: the text is broken. Later Jewish tradition held that Leviathan and Behemoth would be food for the righteous at the end (4 Ezra 6:49–52; 2 Bar 29:4).
The order and wording of verses 24–25 are confused in the manuscripts; this rendering follows the reconstruction generally adopted.

verses.text: In those days I saw long cords handed to those angels. They took wings for themselves and flew off northward.
I asked the angel, “Why have they taken those cords and gone?” He answered, “They have gone off to measure.”

The angel who went with me said,
“These will bring the measurements of the righteous
and the measuring lines of the righteous to the righteous,
so that they may lean on the Lord of Spirits’ name forever and ever.{a}

These measurements will bring to light every secret of the depths of the earth,
those swallowed up by the desert,
those eaten by wild animals,
and those eaten by the fish of the sea,
so that they may come back and find support
on the day of the Chosen One;
for no one will be lost before the Lord of Spirits,
and no one can be lost.”
All who are in the heights of heaven received a command, a power, one voice, and one light like fire.

With their first words they blessed that one,
and they praised and exalted him with wisdom,
showing wisdom in speech and in the spirit of life.

When he raises his face
to judge their hidden ways by the word of the Lord of Spirits’ name,
and their paths by the way of the just judgment of the Lord of Spirits,
then with one voice they will all speak and bless,
glorify, exalt, and hallow the Lord of Spirits’ name.

He will call the whole host of heaven, all the holy ones above, the host of the Lord—the cherubim, the seraphim, and the ophanim,{c} all the angels of power and all the angels of dominion—and the Chosen One, and the other powers that are on the dry ground and over the water.

On that day they will lift a single voice. They will bless, glorify, and exalt in a spirit of faith, of wisdom, of patience, of mercy, of justice and peace, and of goodness, and all will say together, “Blessed is he, and blessed be the Lord of Spirits’ name forever and ever!”

For the Lord of Spirits abounds in mercy and is patient;
all his works and all that he has made
he has revealed to the righteous and the chosen
in the Lord of Spirits’ name.

notes.text: Measurements... measuring lines: images of resurrection and restoration; compare Zech 2:1–5; Ezek 40:3; Rev 11:1.
Placed... on the throne: so some manuscripts; others read “The Lord of Spirits sat on the throne of his glory.”

Cherubim, seraphim, ophanim: classes of heavenly beings. *Cherubim* (Hebrew *keruvim*, meaning uncertain) guard Eden and the ark (Gen 3:24; Exod 25:18–22); *seraphim*, “burning ones” (Isa 6:2); *ophanim*, “wheels” (Ezek 1:15–21; 10:9–13). Compare 71:7.

verses.text: This is what the Lord commanded the kings, the powerful, the exalted, and those who inhabit the dry ground: “Open your eyes and raise your horns,{a} if you can recognize the Chosen One.”

The Lord of Spirits seated him{b} on his glorious throne,
and the spirit of righteousness was poured out on him.
The word of his mouth kills every sinner,
and all the lawless are wiped out before him.{c}

On that day all the kings and the powerful,
the exalted and those who hold the dry ground,
will rise up and see and know
that he sits on his glorious throne;
righteousness is judged in his presence,
and no false word is spoken before him.

Then pain will come over them
like that of a woman in labor
who struggles to give birth
when her child comes to the mouth of the womb.
The kings, the powerful, and all who possess the dry ground will bless, glorify, and exalt the one who rules over everything, who had been hidden.

The community of the chosen and holy will be sown,{e}
and all the chosen will stand before him on that day.

All the kings, the powerful, the exalted, and those who rule the dry ground
will fall face down before him,
worship him, set their hope on that Son of Man,
and beg him and plead for mercy from him.

But the Lord of Spirits will press them so hard
that they will rush from his presence;
their faces will be full of shame,
and darkness will pile up on their faces.

He will hand them over to the angels of punishment
to take vengeance on them,
because they oppressed his children and his chosen ones.

They will be a spectacle for the righteous and for his chosen ones.
They will rejoice over them,
because the anger of the Lord of Spirits rests on them
and his sword is drunk with their blood.{f}

The righteous and chosen will be saved on that day,
and from then on they will never again see the faces of the sinners and the lawless.

The righteous and chosen will have risen from the earth
and will no longer go about with downcast faces.

They will be dressed in garments of glory,
garments of life from the Lord of Spirits.
Your garments will not wear out,
and your glory will not fade before the Lord of Spirits.{g}

notes.text: Raise your horns: an idiom for showing strength or pride (Ps 75:4–5).
Seated him: so with a slight change; the manuscripts read “sat on.”
Compare Isa 11:2, 4; Ps Sol 17:24; Rev 19:15.

Son of a Woman: Ge'ez *walda be'si*, “son of a man” in most manuscripts; some read *walda 'eguāla 'emma-ḥeyāw*, “son of the offspring of the mother of the living,” that is, of Eve. See the note at 46:2.
Will be sown: that is, will be planted and grow; compare 10:16; 93:2, 5, 10.
Compare Isa 34:5–6; Deut 32:42.
Compare 2 Cor 5:2–4; Rev 3:4–5; 6:11.

verses.text: In those days the powerful and the kings who possess the dry ground will beg his angels of punishment, to whom they have been handed over, to give them a short break, so that they may bow in worship to the Lord of Spirits and acknowledge their sins to him.

They will bless and glorify the Lord of Spirits, saying:
“Blessed is the Lord of Spirits, the Lord of kings,
Lord of the powerful and Lord of the rich,
Lord of glory and Lord of wisdom.

Every hidden thing shines with your power from generation to generation,
and your glory endures forever and ever.
Your secrets are deep and past counting,
and your righteousness is beyond reckoning.

Now we have learned that we ought to glorify
and bless the Lord of kings, the one who is King over all kings.”

They will say, “If only we had a pause to glorify, give thanks,
and confess our faith before his glory!

Now we long for a little rest but do not find it;
we chase it but cannot catch it.
Light has gone from before us,
and darkness is our home forever and ever.

For we did not believe in him
or glorify the Lord of Spirits’ name;
our hope was in the scepter of our kingdom
and in our own splendor.

On the day of our suffering and distress he does not save us,
and we find no break in which to confess
that our Lord is faithful in all his deeds, his judgments, and his justice,
and that his judgments show no partiality.

We vanish from his presence because of our deeds,
and every one of our sins has been counted out exactly.”
Then they will say to themselves, “Our souls are stuffed with ill-gotten wealth, but it does not stop us from going down out of it into the flames of the torment of Sheol.”{a}

After that their faces will be filled with darkness
and shame before that Son of Man;
they will be driven from his presence,
and the sword will stay before him among them.
So says the Lord of Spirits: “This is the decree and the judgment against the powerful, the kings, the exalted, and those who possess the dry ground, in the presence of the Lord of Spirits.”

notes.text: The flames of the torment of Sheol: so some manuscripts; others read “the weight” or “the burden of Sheol.” Compare Luke 16:23–24.

verses.text: I saw other figures hidden in that place.
I heard the angel’s voice say, “These are the angels who came down to the earth, disclosed hidden things to humankind, and led human beings into sin.”
In those days Noah{a} saw that the earth had tilted and that its ruin was near.
He got up from there and went to the ends of the earth and cried out to his great-grandfather Enoch.{b} In an anguished voice Noah said three times, “Hear me, hear me, hear me!”
I said to him, “Tell me what is happening on the earth, that the earth is so battered and shaken, or I may perish with it.”
Just then there was a great upheaval on the earth; a voice sounded from heaven, and I dropped face down.
My great-grandfather Enoch came and stood beside me and said, “Why have you cried out to me so bitterly and with tears?

A command has gone out from the Lord against those who live on the dry ground, that their end is to be carried out, because they have learned all the secrets of the angels, all the violence of the satans and all their most secret powers, all the power of those who practice sorcery and spells, and the power of those who cast idols for the whole earth;
how silver comes from the dust of the earth, and how soft metal comes into being on the earth.
For lead and tin are not produced from the earth as the first is; there is a spring that produces them, and an angel stands in it, and that angel is prominent.”
After that my great-grandfather Enoch took me by the hand, raised me up, and said to me, “Go, for I have asked the Lord of Spirits about this upheaval on the earth.

He told me, ‘Because of their lawlessness their judgment has been decided, and I will not hold it back any longer. Because of the sorceries they have searched out and learned, the earth and its inhabitants will be destroyed.’

For these there will never be a place of repentance, because they have revealed what was hidden, and they are condemned. But as for you, my son, the Lord of Spirits knows that you are pure and innocent of this blame concerning the secrets.

He has set your name among the holy ones
and will keep you safe among those who live on the dry ground;
he has destined your righteous offspring for kingship and great honor,
and from your offspring will come a spring of the righteous and holy, past counting, forever.”

notes.text: *Noah*: Hebrew *Noaḥ*, connected in Gen 5:29 with *naḥam*, “to comfort,” and with *nuaḥ*, “to rest.” Chapters 65–69:25 are another piece of the Noah tradition (see the note at 54:7); Noah speaks in the first person.
Great-grandfather: so the sense; the text has “grandfather” (Ge'ez uses the word loosely). By Gen 5:21–29 Enoch is Noah’s great-grandfather: Enoch, Methuselah, Lamech, Noah.

verses.text: After that he showed me the angels of punishment who are ready to come and unleash all the forces of the water that lies under the earth, to bring judgment and destruction on all who live on the dry ground.
The Lord of Spirits ordered the angels who were going out not to raise the waters but to hold them back, for those angels were in charge of the forces of the waters.
Then I left Enoch’s presence.
In those days the word of God came to me, and he said to me, “Noah, your lot has come up before me, a lot free of blame, a lot of love and uprightness.

Now the angels are building a wooden structure,{a} and when they have finished the task I will lay my hand on it and keep it safe. From it will come the seed of life, and a change will take place, so that the earth will not be left empty.

I will establish your offspring before me forever and ever, and I will scatter abroad those who live with you. It will not be barren on the face of the dry ground, but it will be blessed and will multiply on the earth in the name of the Lord.”

He will lock up those angels who displayed lawlessness in that burning valley that my great-grandfather Enoch had shown me earlier in the west, near the mountains of gold, silver, iron, soft metal, and tin.{b}
I saw that valley, in which there was a great churning and a heaving of the waters.

When all this happened, from that fiery molten metal and from the churning in that place, a smell of sulfur arose and mixed with those waters. That valley of the angels who had led people astray burned beneath that ground.
Through its valleys flow rivers of fire, where those angels are punished who led astray the inhabitants of the dry ground.

But in those days those waters will serve the kings, the powerful, the exalted, and those who live on the dry ground for the healing of body and soul,{c} and for the punishment of the spirit. Their spirits are full of lust, so that they will be punished in their bodies, for they have denied the Lord of Spirits. They see their punishment every day, yet they do not believe in his name.
As the burning of their bodies grows fierce, a matching change will come over their spirits forever and ever, for no one will speak an idle word before the Lord of Spirits.
For judgment will come on them, because they trust in the lust of their bodies and deny the Spirit of the Lord.

Those same waters will change in those days. When those angels are punished in these waters, the springs will change their heat; and when the angels come up, the spring water will change and turn cold.
I heard Michael respond, “This judgment by which the angels are judged is a witness against the kings and the powerful who possess the dry ground.
For these waters of judgment serve the healing of the kings’ bodies and the lust of their bodies; so they will not see or believe that those waters will change and become a fire that burns forever.”

notes.text: A wooden structure: the ark (Gen 6:14–16). Here angels build it.
Compare 52:2 and 53:1; 54:1.

Healing of body and soul: so the manuscripts; Charles emends to “for the healing of the body, but for the punishment of the spirit.” The hot springs may allude to those used by Herod the Great at Callirrhoe by the Dead Sea, about 4 BC (Josephus, *Antiquities* 17.171–173).

verses.text: After that my great-grandfather Enoch instructed me in every secret contained in the book of the discourses that had been given to him, and he gathered them for me into the words of the book of the discourses.

On that day Michael spoke up and said to Raphael, “The force of the spirit carries me away and makes me tremble at the severity of the judgment of the secrets, the judgment of the angels. Who can bear the harsh judgment that has been carried out, before which they melt?”

Again Michael spoke up and said to Raphael, “Who would not be softened in heart about it, and whose insides would not be troubled by this word of judgment passed against them, against those whom they have led out like this?”

When he stood before the Lord of Spirits, Michael said to Raphael, “I will not take their side under the eye of the Lord, for the Lord of Spirits is angry with them because they behave as if they were the Lord.
That is why everything hidden will come upon them forever and ever. Neither angel nor human will have a share in it; they alone have received their judgment forever and ever.”
After this judgment they will terrify them and make them tremble, because they revealed this to those who live on the dry ground.

Here are the names of those angels.{a} The first of them is Semyaza; the second Artaqifa; the third Armen; the fourth Kokabel; the fifth Turael; the sixth Rumyal; the seventh Danyal; the eighth Neqael; the ninth Baraqel; the tenth Azazel; the eleventh Armaros; the twelfth Batryal; the thirteenth Basasael; the fourteenth Ananel; the fifteenth Turel; the sixteenth Simapesiel; the seventeenth Yetrel; the eighteenth Tumael; the nineteenth Turel; the twentieth Rumael; the twenty-first Azazel.
These are the leaders of their angels and their names, their chiefs over hundreds, over fifties, and over tens.
The name of the first is Yeqon.{b} He is the one who led all the children of God astray, brought them down to the earth, and misled them through the daughters of humankind.
The second is named Asbeel. He gave evil counsel to the holy children of God and misled them into defiling their bodies with human women.

The third is named Gadreel. He is the one who showed human beings every deadly blow. He led Eve astray,{c} and showed human beings the weapons of death: shield, breastplate, and sword for battle, and every weapon of death.
From his hand they have gone out against those who live on the dry ground from that day and forever.
The fourth is named Penemue. He taught human beings bitter and sweet, and taught them all the secrets of their wisdom.
He showed people how to write with ink and paper,{d} and through this many have sinned from age to age until this day.
Human beings were not created for this, to confirm their good faith with pen and ink.

For humans were created no differently from the angels, to stay righteous and pure, and death, which ruins everything, would not have touched them. But through this knowledge of theirs they are perishing, and through this power it is devouring me.{e}

The fifth is named Kasdeya. He showed human beings all the evil blows of spirits and demons: the blows that strike the embryo in the womb so that it miscarries, the bites of the snake, and the blows that come in the midday heat, the snake’s offspring, whose name is Tabaet.{f}
This is Kasbeel’s task: he is chief of the oath, which he disclosed to the holy ones while he dwelt in the glory on high; its name is Biqa.
This one asked Michael to show him the hidden name, so that he might pronounce it in the oath, so that those who revealed every secret thing to humankind would tremble before that name and oath.
Such is the force of this oath, mighty and strong. He put this oath, Akae, in Michael’s hand.

These are the secrets of this oath,
and they are made firm by his oath:
heaven was hung up before the world was created,
and forever.

By it the earth was founded on the water,
and from the hidden places of the mountains come lovely waters,
from the creation of the world and forever.

By that oath the depths are made fast;
they stay and do not move from their place, from age to age.

By that oath the sun and moon complete their courses
and do not swerve from their decree, from age to age.
So too the spirits of the water and of the winds, of all the breezes, and their paths from every quarter of the winds.
There the voices of the thunder and the light of the lightning are kept, and there the storerooms of the hail and of the frost are kept, the storerooms of the mist and of the rain and dew.

All of them believe and offer thanks to the Lord of Spirits and give him glory with all their might; their food is all thanksgiving. They thank, glorify, and exalt the Lord of Spirits’ name forever and ever.

He sat on his glorious throne,
and the whole of judgment was handed over to the Son of Man.{i}
He makes the sinners vanish and be destroyed from the face of the earth,
together with those who led the world astray.

They will be bound with chains
and locked up in the gathering place of their destruction,
and all their works will vanish from the face of the earth.

From then on nothing will be corruptible,
for that Son of Man has come into view
and is seated on his glorious throne.
All evil will pass away before him,
and the word of that Son of Man will go out
and prevail before the Lord of Spirits.
Here ends Enoch’s third discourse.

notes.text: This list largely repeats 6:7, in corrupted Ethiopic forms; compare the notes there. *Shemihazah* appears as *Semyaza*; *Asael* appears twice (as *Azazel*).

*Yeqon*: perhaps “he will incite” (Hebrew *yaqum*, “he rises”). *Asbeel*: perhaps “deserter from God.” *Gadreel*: “God is my helper” or “wall of God.” *Penemue*: perhaps “inside” or “face.” *Kasdeya*: “Chaldean,” recalling the Chaldeans as experts in magic and astrology. *Kasbeel*: perhaps “deceiver of God.” *Biqa*: perhaps “request” or “the one who asks.” *Akae*: meaning unknown; some connect it with *ʾ-k-y*, “to name.”
He led Eve astray: here the serpent of Gen 3 is identified with a fallen angel; compare Wis 2:24; Rev 12:9.
Paper: papyrus. Writing itself is here counted among the forbidden arts, in contrast to Enoch the scribe (12:4) and to Jubilees 4:17, where Enoch is the first to learn writing.
It is devouring me: perhaps “death is devouring us”; the text is uncertain.
Midday heat: compare Ps 91:6. *Tabaet*: perhaps “male” or “strong”; the meaning is uncertain.
Compare Job 38:8–11; Jer 5:22.
Compare Isa 40:26; Bar 3:34–35.
Compare John 5:22, 27.

verses.text: After this, while he was still alive, his name was lifted up into the presence of that Son of Man and into the presence of the Lord of Spirits, away from those who live on the dry ground.{a}
He was raised on the chariots of the wind,{b} and his name departed from among them.

From that day I was no longer counted among them. He set me between two winds, between north and west, where the angels had taken the cords to mark out for me a place for the chosen and the righteous.
There I saw the first ancestors and the righteous who from the beginning have lived in that place.

notes.text: Chapters 70–71 describe Enoch’s final removal from earth; compare Gen 5:24, “Enoch walked with God, and he was no more, for God took him.” The narrative shifts from third person (70:1–2) to first person (70:3).
The chariots of the wind: or “of the spirit”; compare Elijah in 2 Kgs 2:11.

verses.text:
He showed me all the secrets of the ends of heaven,
all the storerooms of all the stars and all the lights,
from where they come out before the holy ones.

I saw angels past counting,
thousands upon thousands and myriads upon myriads,
surrounding that house.
Michael, Raphael, Gabriel, and Phanuel,
and the holy angels in heaven above,
go in and out of that house.

Out of that house came Michael and Gabriel, Raphael and Phanuel,
and many holy angels beyond number,

and the Head of Days came with them,
his head pure and white like wool,
his robes past describing.

I fell on my face;
my whole body went limp,
and my spirit was transformed.
I cried out in a loud voice,
with a spirit of power,
and I blessed, glorified, and exalted.
These blessings that came from my mouth pleased that Head of Days.

That Head of Days came, accompanied by Michael, Gabriel, Raphael, and Phanuel,
and thousands and myriads of angels past counting.

He{d} came to me, greeted me with his voice, and said to me,
“You are that son of man{e} who was born for righteousness;
righteousness rests on you,
and the righteousness of the Head of Days will not abandon you.”

He said to me,
“He proclaims peace to you in the name of the age to come,
for from there peace has gone out since the creation of the world,
and so you will have it forever and ever and ever.

Everyone will walk in your ways,
since righteousness will never abandon you;
with you will be their homes, and with you their inheritance,
and they will not be parted from you forever and ever and ever.

So with that son of man there will be long life,
and the righteous will have peace and an upright way
in the Lord of Spirits’ name forever and ever.”

notes.text: The children of God: angels; compare 6:2; Job 1:6.
Hyacinth: a precious stone, probably blue (sapphire or jacinth).
Crystals: or “hailstones”; compare 14:9–10.
He: the angel, or perhaps the Head of Days himself. Charles assumes a passage has been lost before this verse and changes “you” to “this.”

You are that son of man: so all the Ethiopic manuscripts. Here Enoch himself is identified with the heavenly figure of the Parables, or, as many read it, is simply called “a human being born for righteousness” (compare 60:10). Charles and some translators emend to “This is the Son of Man.” This translation follows the manuscripts.

verses.text: The book of the movements of the lights of heaven, each as it is, by their kinds, their authority, and their seasons, by their names and their places of rising, and by their months, which Uriel, the holy angel who was with me and who is their guide, showed me. He showed me their whole design exactly as it is, for every year of the world and forever, until the new creation is made that lasts forever.{a}
This is the first law of the lights. The light called the sun rises in the eastern gates of heaven and sets in the western gates of heaven.

I saw six gates where the sun rises and six gates where the sun sets. The moon also rises and sets in these gates, as do the leaders of the stars with those they lead: six in the east and six in the west, all lined up exactly, one after another. There are also many windows to the right and left of these gates.{b}
First the great light named the sun comes out. Its circle is like the circle of heaven, and it is entirely full of fire that gives light and heat.

The wind drives the chariot on which it rides up. The sun goes down out of the sky and turns back by way of the north to reach the east, and it is guided so that it arrives at the proper gate and shines in the face of the sky.
In this way it rises in the first month{c} in the great gate, which is the fourth of those six gates in the east.
In that fourth gate, from which the sun rises in the first month, there are twelve window openings, from which flame comes out when they are opened at their time.
When the sun rises in the sky, it comes out through that fourth gate for thirty mornings in a row and sets exactly in the fourth gate in the west of the sky.
Through this period each day grows longer and each night shorter, until the thirtieth morning.
By then daylight exceeds darkness by one ninth: the day comes to exactly ten parts and the night to eight.{d}
The sun rises from that fourth gate and sets in the fourth, then moves to the fifth gate of the east for thirty mornings, rising from it and setting in the fifth gate.
Then the day grows longer by two parts and comes to eleven parts, and the night grows shorter and comes to seven parts.{e}
It returns to the east and enters the sixth gate, and rises and sets in the sixth gate for thirty-one mornings, because of its sign.{f}
On that day the day is longer than the night, so that the day is twice the night: the day becomes twelve parts, and the night is cut back to six parts.
Then the sun rises so as to make the day shorter and the night longer. The sun goes back to the east and enters the sixth gate, and rises and sets from it for thirty mornings.
When the thirty mornings are over, the day has lost exactly one part and is eleven parts, and the night seven.
The sun leaves that sixth gate in the west, goes to the east, and rises in the fifth gate for thirty mornings, and sets again in the west in the fifth western gate.
On that day the day has lost two parts; the day comes to ten parts and the night to eight.
The sun leaves that fifth gate and sets in the fifth gate of the west, and rises in the fourth gate for thirty-one mornings because of its sign, and sets in the west.
On that day the day equals the night; they are of equal length, the night nine parts and the day nine.{g}
The sun rises from that gate and sets in the west, then returns to the east and rises in the third gate for thirty mornings and sets in the west in the third gate.

On that day the night grows longer than the day, each night longer than the last and each day shorter than the last until the thirtieth morning; the night comes to exactly ten parts and the day to eight.

Leaving the third gate, where it rose and set in the west, the sun goes back east and rises out of the second eastern gate for thirty mornings, and likewise sets in the second gate in the west of the sky.
On that day the night comes to eleven parts and the day to seven.

On that day the sun rises from that second gate and sets in the west in the second gate, and returns to the east into the first gate for thirty-one mornings, and sets in the first gate in the west of the sky.
On that day the night grows long and becomes double the day: the night is exactly twelve parts and the day six.{h}
With that the sun has gone through the stages of its circuit, and it turns back over those same stages: it enters that gate for thirty mornings and sets also in the west opposite it.
That night the night has shortened by a ninth, to eleven parts, and the day is seven parts.
The sun comes back and enters the second gate in the east and returns over those stages of its circuit for thirty mornings, rising and setting.
On that day the night shortens: the night comes to ten parts and the day to eight.
On that day the sun rises from that gate and sets in the west, returns to the east, and rises in the third gate for thirty-one mornings, and sets in the west of the sky.
On that day the night has shortened to nine parts and the day is nine parts; night equals day, and the year comes to exactly three hundred and sixty-four days.{i}
The lengthening of the day and the night, and the shortening of the day and the night, all come about through the sun’s course; by it they are made different.
So its course grows longer by day and shorter by night.{j}
This is the law and course of the sun and its return, as often as it returns: sixty times it rises and goes back.{k} That is, the great light called the sun, forever and ever.
What rises in this way is the great light, and it is named by its appearance, as the Lord commanded.
As it rises, so it sets; it does not grow less and does not rest, but runs day and night. Its light is seven times brighter than the moon’s, but in size the two are equal.

notes.text: This section, often called the Astronomical Book or the Book of the Luminaries, is the oldest part of 1 Enoch; Aramaic fragments of a longer form (4QEnastr a–d) are reported to date from about 200 BC or earlier. It sets out a schematic solar year of 364 days: exactly 52 weeks, divided into four quarters of 91 days, each made of two 30-day months and one 31-day month. Because 364 is divisible by 7, every date falls on the same day of the week every year, and festivals never fall on a sabbath. The same calendar is defended in Jubilees and was used by the Qumran community. It runs about 1¼ days short of the true solar year (about 365.24 days); the text never addresses the gap.

The six gates: the horizon is divided into six sectors on each side, east and west, through which the sun moves north and south over the year. Gate 1 is the southernmost (the sun’s rising point at midwinter) and gate 6 the northernmost (at midsummer). The sun spends 30 days in each gate, or 31 at the four turning points, making 364.
The first month: the month beginning at the spring equinox, roughly late March to late April. This calendar starts the year in spring, as in Exod 12:2.

Parts: the text divides the whole day-and-night into 18 equal parts, so that one part equals 80 minutes. Here the day is 10 parts (13 hours 20 minutes) and the night 8 (10 hours 40 minutes). At the equinoxes each is 9 parts (12 hours); at midsummer the day reaches 12 parts (16 hours) and the night 6 (8 hours). This 2 : 1 ratio of longest to shortest day fits a latitude well north of Judea and was common in Babylonian astronomy.
Eleven parts: 14 hours 40 minutes; seven parts: 9 hours 20 minutes.
Because of its sign: the extra 31st day marks a turning point of the year, here the summer solstice, about June 21.
The autumn equinox, about September 22: day and night are each 12 hours.
The winter solstice, about December 21: night 16 hours, day 8 hours.
The spring equinox, about March 20, completing the year: 30 + 30 + 31 days in each of four quarters = 364 days.
The sense of this verse is obscure in the manuscripts.
Sixty times: perhaps meaning the sun passes through each pair of gates twice a year, once going north and once going south (6 × 2 × 5?), or the figure is corrupt. Its meaning is uncertain.

verses.text: After this law I saw another law, concerning the lesser light, called the moon.
Its circle is like the circle of heaven, and the chariot on which it rides is driven by the wind, and light is given to it by measure.
Its rising and setting shift every month, and its days are like the days of the sun. When its light is complete, it is a seventh of the sun’s light.

This is how it rises. Its first phase comes out in the east on the thirtieth morning. On that day it becomes visible and marks for you the start of the month on the thirtieth day, together with the sun, in the gate where the sun rises.
Half of it stands out by a seventh, and its whole disk is empty, without light, except for a seventh of it, a fourteenth part of its light.{a}
When it receives a seventh of half its light, its light comes to a seventh and a half.

It sets with the sun. When the sun rises, the moon rises with it and receives half of one part of light. On that night, at the beginning of its day, the moon sets with the sun and is unseen that night, with its fourteen and a half parts.
On that day it rises with exactly a seventh, comes out and moves away from the sunrise, and in its remaining days it grows bright in the other thirteen parts.

notes.text: The moon’s light is counted in fourteenths (or sevenths and their halves). Over 14 or 15 days it gains its light in steps and loses it again in the same steps.

verses.text: I saw another course and law for the moon, how by that law it makes its monthly circuit.

Uriel, the holy angel who leads them all, showed me all of this and their positions. I recorded where they stood just as he pointed them out, and recorded their months as they are and how their light appears, until fifteen days are completed.
By sevenths it completes all its light in the east, and by sevenths it completes all its darkness in the west.
In certain months it shifts its settings, and in certain months it follows a course of its own.
For two months the moon and sun go down together through the two middle gates, the third and the fourth.

It goes out for seven days, turns, and comes back again through the gate where the sun rises and completes all its light. Then it moves away from the sun and in eight days enters the sixth gate, from which the sun comes out.

When the sun comes out of the fourth gate, the moon goes out for seven days until it comes out of the fifth, then turns back again in seven days to the fourth gate and completes all its light; then it moves away and enters the first gate in eight days.
It comes back again in seven days to the fourth gate, from which the sun comes out.
That is how I saw them placed: the rising of the moons and the setting of the sun during those days.
If five years are added together, the sun has a surplus of thirty days; and all the days that fall to it for one of those five years, when they are complete, come to 364 days.
The surplus of the sun and the stars comes to six days: in five years, at six days a year, that makes thirty days, and the moon falls behind the sun and the stars by thirty days.{a}
Sun and stars usher in every year precisely, so that their position never moves ahead or falls behind by a single day, forever; they complete the years with perfect fairness in 364 days.
In three years there are 1,092 days, and in five years 1,820 days, so that in eight years there are 2,912 days.{b}
For the moon alone the days in three years come to 1,062, and in five years it falls fifty days behind.{c}
In five years there are 1,770 days, so that for the moon the days in eight years come to 2,832.
In eight years it falls behind by eighty days; all the days it falls behind in eight years are eighty.{d}
The year is completed exactly according to their stations in the world and the stations of the sun, which rise from the gates through which it rises and sets for thirty days.

notes.text: The lunar year of twelve months of 29 or 30 days is 354 days, ten days shorter than the 364-day solar year; the text here rounds the yearly difference to six days by a different reckoning, and the figures in verses 10–16 do not all agree. The manuscripts vary in the numbers.
3 × 354 = 1,062, thirty days short of the solar total; in five years 1,770, fifty short.

verses.text: The leaders of the chiefs of thousands, who are placed over all creation and over all the stars, are also bound up with the four added days.{a} They cannot be separated from their posts, according to the reckoning of the year, and they serve on the four days that are not counted in the reckoning of the year.

Because of them people go wrong, for those lights truly serve at the stations of the world: one in the first gate, one in the third gate of heaven, one in the fourth gate, and one in the sixth gate. The year is completed exactly through its 364 separate stations.{b}

For Uriel the angel showed me the signs, the seasons, the years, and the days—Uriel, whom the Lord of glory has set forever over all the lights of heaven, in heaven and in the world, so that they may rule over the face of the sky and be seen on the earth and be leaders of the day and the night: the sun, the moon, the stars, and all the serving creatures that make their circuit in all the chariots of heaven.{c}

Likewise Uriel showed me twelve doors open in the circle of the sun’s chariot in the sky, through which the sun’s rays break out. From them warmth spreads over the earth when they are opened at their appointed times;
They serve also the winds and the spirit of dew, when they open, standing wide at the edges of the heavens.
As for the twelve gates of the sky at the earth’s edges: from them the sun, moon, and stars and everything made in the heavens come forth, eastward and westward.

Many windows are open to their left and right, and one window at its time sends out warmth, matching those doors from which the stars come out as he has commanded them, and in which they set according to their number.
I saw chariots in the sky running through the world above those gates, in which turn the stars that never set.
One is larger than all the rest, and it makes its circuit through the whole world.{d}

notes.text: The four added days: the four 31st days, one at the end of each quarter (the equinoxes and solstices), which bring 360 up to 364.
People go wrong: the author attacks those who used a 360-day year or a lunar calendar; compare 82:4–6 and Jubilees 6:32–38.
Compare Gen 1:14–18.
One is larger: perhaps the Great Bear (the Big Dipper), which never sets at northern latitudes; compare “the Bear” in Job 9:9; 38:32.

verses.text: At the ends of the earth I saw twelve gates open toward all the quarters, from which the winds come out and blow over the earth.
Three of them open on the face of the sky, three toward the west, three on the right of the sky, and three on the left.{a}
The first three are those of the east, then three of the north, then three of the south, and three of the west.

Through four of them come winds of blessing and well-being, and from the other eight come harmful winds. When these are sent, they bring destruction on the whole earth, on the water on it, on all who live on it, and on everything in the water and on the land.
The first wind from those gates, called the east wind, comes out through the first gate in the east, the one leaning toward the south. From it come desolation, drought, heat, and ruin.
Through the second gate, in the middle, comes what is right: from it come rain, fruitfulness, well-being, and dew. Through the third gate, toward the north, come cold and drought.
After these come the south winds, through three gates. Through the first of them, leaning toward the east, a hot wind comes out.
Through the middle gate next to it come sweet smells, dew and rain, well-being and health.
Through the third gate, toward the west, come dew and rain, locusts and desolation.
After these come the north winds. From the seventh gate, on the east side, come dew and rain, locusts and desolation.
From the middle gate come, straight on, health and rain, dew and well-being. Through the third gate, on the west side, come mist and frost, snow and rain, dew and locusts.
After these four come the west winds. Through the first gate, next to the north, come dew and frost, cold, snow, and ice.
From the middle gate come dew and rain, well-being and blessing. Through the last gate, next to the south, come drought and desolation, burning and ruin.
So the twelve gates of the four quarters of heaven are finished. All their laws, all their plagues, and all their benefits I have shown you, my son Methuselah.{b}

notes.text: The face of the sky: the east. In Semitic orientation one faces east, so “right” is south and “left” is north.
*Methuselah*: Hebrew *Metushelaḥ*, perhaps “man of the javelin” or “man of Shelah.” Enoch’s son (Gen 5:21–27), to whom the Astronomical Book and the Epistle are addressed.

verses.text: The east is named as the first quarter, since it comes first.{a} The second is called the south, because the Most High will come down there; there especially the one who is blessed forever will come down.
The west quarter is called “the waning,” because there all the lights of heaven wane and go down.

The fourth quarter, called the north, is divided into three: the first part is for human habitation; the second holds seas of water, the deeps, forests, rivers, darkness, and mist; and the third part holds the garden of righteousness.
I saw seven high mountains, higher than all the mountains on the earth; from there frost comes out, and days, seasons, and years pass away.
I saw seven rivers on the earth, larger than all other rivers. One of them comes from the west and pours its waters into the Great Sea.{b}
Two flow down from the north and empty into the Red Sea in the east.
The other four come out on the north side to their own sea: two of them to the Red Sea, and two into the Great Sea, where they empty; some say, into the desert.
I saw seven great islands in the sea and on the land: two on the land and five in the Great Sea.{c}

notes.text: The quarter names are wordplays in Aramaic or Hebrew: east, *qedem*, also means “first, before”; south, *darom*, is explained as *dar rum*, “the Exalted One dwells,” here “the Most High will descend there”; west, *maʿarav*, is linked with *ʿarav*, “to go down, wane”; north, *tsafon*, with *tsafun*, “hidden.”

The Great Sea: the Mediterranean. *The Red Sea*: the *Erythraean Sea*, the waters south and east of Arabia (see the note at 32:2). The rivers may be the Nile, Tigris, Euphrates, and others known to ancient geographers.
Charles counts this as 77:8; some editions number it 77:9.

verses.text: These are the names of the sun: the first Oryares, and the second Tomas.{a}
The moon has four names: the first is Asonya, the second Ebla, the third Benase, and the fourth Erae.
These are the two great lights. Their circle is like the circle of heaven, and the two circles are the same size.
In the circle of the sun there are seven portions of light more than in the moon, and these are passed on in fixed amounts until the seventh portion of the sun is used up.
They set and go into the western gates, make their circuit by way of the north, and come out through the eastern gates on the face of the sky.
When the moon rises, a fourteenth part appears in the sky, and on the fourteenth day it completes its light.
Fifteen parts of light are passed to it until the fifteenth day, when its light is completed according to the sign of the year; it becomes fifteen parts, and the moon grows by fourteenths.

As it wanes it loses one part a day: fourteen parts remain after day one, thirteen after day two, then twelve, eleven, ten, nine, eight, seven, six, five, four, three, and two by day thirteen; by day fourteen only half a seventh is left, and by day fifteen the last of its light is gone.
Some months last twenty-nine days, and one lasts twenty-eight.
Uriel showed me another law: when light is passed to the moon, and from which side the sun passes it.
All the time the moon is growing in its light, it is drawing it to itself while facing the sun, for fourteen days, until it is lit all over and its light is complete in the sky.
Its first day bears the name new moon, since light first dawns on it then.
It becomes full exactly on the day the sun sets in the west; it rises from the east at night and shines all night long until the sun rises opposite it, and the moon is seen opposite the sun.
On the side from which the moon’s light comes, it wanes again there until all the light is gone and all the days of the month are finished, and its disk is empty, without light.
It makes three months of thirty days, and at its time it makes three months of twenty-nine days each, in which it completes its waning in the first period, in the first gate, for 177 days.{b}
As it goes out, it shows itself through three thirty-day months and three twenty-nine-day months.
At night it looks like a man for twenty days each time,{c} and by day it looks like the sky, for there is nothing else in it but its light.

notes.text: The names of the sun and moon are of uncertain origin. *Oryares* may come from Hebrew *ʾor ḥeres*, “light of the sun”; *Tomas* perhaps from Hebrew *ḥammah*, “heat,” or Aramaic. Of the moon’s names, *Asonya*, *Ebla*, *Benase*, and *Erae* may reflect Hebrew *ʾishon*, “pupil (of the eye),” *levanah*, “white one,” *ben ḥese*, “son of the full moon,” and *yareaḥ*, “moon.” All are guesses.
177 days: 3 × 30 + 3 × 29 = 177, half of a lunar year of 354 days.
Like a man: perhaps the “man in the moon”; the text is uncertain.

verses.text: Now, my son, I have shown you everything, and the law of all the stars of heaven is complete.
He showed me all their laws for every day, for every season of rule, for every year and its going out, and for the order set for it every month and every week;
and the waning of the moon that takes place in the sixth gate, for in this sixth gate its light is completed, and after that the waning begins;
and the waning that takes place in the first gate in its season, until 177 days are completed, which, counted in weeks, are twenty-five weeks and two days.{a}
It falls behind the sun and the order of the stars by exactly five days in the course of one period,{b} when this place that you see has been passed through.
This is the picture and outline of every light, which Uriel the archangel, their leader, showed me.

notes.text: One period: half a year; 182 − 177 = 5. Compare 74:10–16.

verses.text: At that time Uriel the angel spoke to me in reply: “Look, Enoch, I have shown you everything. I have revealed everything to you, so that you may behold the sun and the moon, the guides of heaven’s stars, and all who turn them, their tasks, their times, and their departures.

In those times the fruit of the earth will be late
and will not grow at its proper time,
and the fruit of the trees will be held back in its season.

The moon will change its order
and will not appear at its time.

In those days the sun will be seen, and it will travel in the evening at the edge of the great chariot in the west,
and will shine more brightly than the order of light allows.

Many chiefs of the stars will break the order,
will change their circuits and their tasks,
and will not appear at the times set for them.

The whole order of the stars will be hidden from the sinners,
and the thoughts of those on the earth will go wrong about them;
they will turn away from all their ways,
they will err and take them for gods.

Evil will multiply upon them,
and punishment will come on them
to destroy them all.”

He said to me,
“Look, Enoch, at these heavenly tablets;{a}
read what is written on them,
and take note of every single thing.”
I looked at the heavenly tablets and read everything written there and understood it all. I read the book of all human deeds and of all mortals who will be on the earth to the farthest generations.

At once I blessed the great Lord, the King of glory forever, for having made all the works of the world.
I praised the Lord for his patience,
and blessed him on account of the children of humankind.

After that I said,
“Happy is the one who dies in righteousness and goodness,
about whom no book of wrongdoing has been written
and against whom no day of judgment will be found.”

Those seven holy ones{b} brought me and set me on the earth in front of the door of my house, and said to me, “Tell everything to your son Methuselah, and show all your children that no human being is righteous before the Lord, for he is the one who made them.

We will leave you with your son for one year, until you give your instructions, so that you may teach your children, write things down for them, and bear witness to all your children. In the second year they will take you from among them.{c}

Let your heart be strong,
for the good will announce righteousness to the good;
the righteous will rejoice with the righteous
and congratulate one another.

But sinners will die with sinners,
and the apostate will go down with the apostate.

Those who do right will die because of human deeds
and be gathered in because of the deeds of the wicked.”
Then they stopped speaking with me, and I went back among my people, praising the Lord of the world.

notes.text: The heavenly tablets: a heavenly record of all that will happen and of God’s laws, prominent also in Jubilees (for example 3:10; 5:13). Compare Ps 139:16; Dan 10:21.
Those seven holy ones: the seven archangels of 20:1–8.
Compare 82:1 and chapters 91 and 106–107, where Enoch instructs Methuselah.

verses.text: Now, my son Methuselah, I am telling you all these things and writing them down for you. I have revealed everything to you and given you books about all of them. So keep safe, my son Methuselah, the books from your father’s hand, and pass them on to the generations of the world.

I have given wisdom to you and your children,
and to the children you will have,
so that they in turn hand it on to their own children through the generations,
a wisdom past their understanding.

Those who understand it will not sleep,
but will keep their ears open to learn this wisdom,
and it will please those who eat it more than fine food.

Happy are all the righteous! Happy are all who walk in the way of righteousness and do not sin as the sinners do in counting all their days, the days in which the sun crosses the sky, going in and out of each gate for thirty days alongside the chiefs of thousands who order the stars, and with the four extra days that split the year into quarters, which guide them and go in with them on those four days.
Because of these, people will go wrong and will not count them in the full reckoning of the year; they will go wrong and not recognize them accurately.
They are part of the year’s count and stand written truly forever: in gates one, three, four, and six, one day apiece, so that the year is filled out at 364 days.

Its account is accurate and its recorded reckoning exact, for Uriel showed me and revealed to me the lights, the months, the festivals, the years, and the days—Uriel, to whom the Lord of all the creation of the world has subjected the host of heaven.
He has authority over night and day in heaven, to make the light shine on human beings: sun, moon, and stars, and all the powers of heaven that turn in their circling chariots.
Here are the ranks of the stars that go down each in its place, its season, its festival, and its month.
Here also are the names of their guides, who see to it that each comes in on time, by rank and season and month, in its term of rule and its station.

First come in the four leaders who split the year into quarters; next the twelve rank-leaders who apportion the months; then, for the 360 days, chiefs of thousands who apportion the days; and for the four extra days, leaders who mark off the quarters.
These chiefs of thousands are slotted in between one leader and the next, each following a station, while the leaders themselves do the dividing.
These are the names of the leaders who divide the four appointed parts of the year: Milkiel, Helemmelek, Meleyal, and Narel.{a}

Their guides are named Adnarel, Iyasusael, and Elomeel. These three come after the rank-leaders, and one more comes after those three, who in turn come after the station-leaders that mark off the quarters of the year.
At the beginning of the year Melkeyal rises first and rules; he is called Tamaini and “sun.” All the days of his rule while he governs are ninety-one days.{b}

These are the signs of the days to be seen on earth in the days of his rule: sweat, heat, and calm. All the trees bear fruit and put out leaves; the wheat is harvested; the roses bloom, and all the flowers that come up in the field; but the trees of winter wither.{c}
These are the names of the leaders under them: Berkael, Zelebsel, and another chief of a thousand who is added, called Hiluyaseph. And the days of this one’s rule are ended.
The next leader after him is Helemmelek, whom they call “the shining sun.” All the days of his light are ninety-one days.{d}

These are the signs of his days on the earth: scorching heat and dryness. The trees ripen their fruit and bring all their fruit to ripeness and readiness; the sheep mate and conceive; all the fruit of the earth is gathered in, and everything in the fields, and the winepress. These things happen in the days of his rule.

These are the names, the orders, and the leaders of those chiefs of thousands: Gidaiyal, Keel, and Heel, and the name of the chief of a thousand added to them is Asfael. And the days of his rule are ended.{e}

notes.text: *Milkiel*: “my king is God.” *Helemmelek*: perhaps “the king’s companion” or “the king is strong.” *Meleyal*: “fullness of God.” *Narel*: “light of God” or “fire of God.” The names of the lesser leaders are of uncertain meaning.
Ninety-one days: one quarter of the 364-day year. Beginning at the spring equinox, this first quarter runs roughly from late March to late June.
The wheat harvest in the land of Israel falls in May–June.
The second quarter, roughly late June to late September.
The book breaks off here; the leaders of the third and fourth quarters are not given.

verses.text: Now, my son Methuselah, I will show you all the visions I have seen, telling them to you one by one.{a}

I saw two visions before I married, and they were quite unlike each other. The first came while I was learning to write; the second, before I married your mother, was a fearful vision. About them I prayed to the Lord.
I had lain down to sleep at my grandfather Mahalalel’s house{b} and in a vision I watched the sky give way, torn loose and falling onto the earth.

As it fell on the earth, I saw the earth swallowed in a vast abyss. Mountains hung upon mountains, hills sank down onto hills, and tall trees were ripped from their trunks, flung down, and sunk in the abyss.
Then a word came into my mouth, and I raised my voice and cried out, “The earth is destroyed!”
My grandfather Mahalalel, who was lying near me, woke me and asked, “Why are you crying out like this, my son? Why such wailing?”

I told him the whole vision I had seen, and he said to me, “You have seen something terrible, my son. Your dream vision is grave; it concerns the secrets of all the earth’s sin. The earth must sink into the abyss and be utterly destroyed.
Now, my son, get up and plead with the Lord of glory, since you are a man of faith, that a remnant may be left on the earth and that he may not wipe out the whole earth.
My son, all this will come down on the earth from heaven, and there will be vast destruction on the earth.”
After that I got up and prayed, pleaded, and begged, and I wrote down my prayer for the generations of the world. I will show it all to you, my son Methuselah.

When I had gone outside and seen the sky, the sun coming up in the east, the moon going down in the west, a scattering of stars, the whole earth, and all things just as he had known them from the start, I blessed the Lord of judgment and praised him, because he had made the sun come out of the windows of the east, so that it climbed and rose over the face of the sky and set out and went on along the path appointed for it.

notes.text: The Book of Dreams (chapters 83–90) contains two dream visions. Aramaic fragments of it are reported from Qumran (4QEn c–f), and it is usually dated to about 165–160 BC, during the Maccabean revolt, because the Animal Apocalypse (chapters 85–90) ends its review of history around that time.
*Mahalalel*: Hebrew *Mahalalʾel*, “praise of God.” Enoch’s great-grandfather in Gen 5:12–18 (Mahalalel, Jared, Enoch); the Ethiopic here calls him grandfather.

verses.text: Lifting my hands in righteousness, I blessed the Holy and Great One. I spoke using my mouth’s breath and the fleshly tongue that God made for human beings to speak with; he gave them breath, a tongue, and a mouth to speak with:

“Blessed are you, Lord, King,
great and mighty in your greatness,
Lord of all the creation of heaven,
King of kings and God of the whole world!
Your power, your kingship, and your greatness last forever and ever,
and your rule through all generations.
All the heavens are your throne forever,
and the whole earth your footstool forever and ever.{a}

For you made all things and you rule all things;
nothing is too hard for you.
Wisdom never leaves the place of your throne
or turns away from your presence.
You know, see, and hear everything,
and nothing is hidden from you, for you see everything.

Now the angels of your heavens have done wrong,
and your anger rests on human flesh
until the great day of judgment.

Now, God and Lord and great King,
I beg and plead with you to grant my prayer:
leave me descendants on the earth;
do not destroy all human flesh
and empty the earth of people,
making the destruction permanent.

Now, my Lord, remove from the earth the flesh that has roused your anger,
but establish the flesh of righteousness and uprightness
as a plant of eternal seed.{b}
Do not hide your face from your servant’s prayer, Lord.”

notes.text: Compare Isa 66:1.
A plant of eternal seed: compare “the plant of righteousness” at 10:16 and 93:2, 5, 10, an image for the faithful remnant of Israel.

verses.text: Later I had a second dream, and I will tell you all of it, my son.
Enoch raised his voice and spoke to his son Methuselah: “I will speak to you, my son. Hear my words, and turn your ear to your father’s dream vision.{a}

Before I married your mother Edna,{b} I saw in a vision on my bed: there was a bull coming out of the earth, and that bull was white.{c} After it came a young cow, and with her came two bulls, one black and the other red.
The black bull gored the red one and chased him across the earth, and after that I could no longer see the red bull.
But the black bull grew, and that young cow went with him. I saw many cattle come from him, looking like him and following him.
That cow, the first one, left the first bull to look for the red one, but did not find him. She mourned bitterly over him and kept searching.
I watched until the first bull came to her and calmed her, and from then on she cried no more.
Next she gave birth to a second white bull,{d} and then to many bulls and black cows.
In my sleep I saw that white bull also grow and become a great white bull, and many white bulls came from him that looked like him.
They began to father many white bulls like themselves, one after another, a great many.

notes.text: Chapters 85–90 are known as the Animal Apocalypse. They retell history from Adam to the end time in symbols: the patriarchs before Jacob are bulls (white for the righteous line, black for the wicked); fallen angels are stars; Israel are sheep; the nations are wild beasts and birds of prey; and angels appear as men. The notes identify each figure as most scholars read it.
*Edna*: perhaps “delight” (Hebrew *ʿednah*). Enoch’s wife, not named in Genesis; Jubilees 4:20 also calls her Edna.
The white bull is Adam; the heifer is Eve; the black and red bulls are Cain and Abel.
Another white bull: Seth (Gen 4:25).

verses.text: Again, as I slept, I looked with my eyes and saw the sky above, and there a star fell from heaven,{a} and it got up, ate, and grazed among those cattle.
After that I saw the large black cattle, and they all changed their stalls, their pastures, and their herds, and began to live together.{b}
Again I looked in the vision toward the sky, and I saw many stars come down and throw themselves from heaven to that first star. They became bulls among those cattle and grazed with them.{c}
I looked at them and saw that they all exposed their organs like stallions and began to mount the cows of the cattle. They all became pregnant and gave birth to elephants, camels, and donkeys.{d}
All the cattle were afraid of them and terrified, and began to bite with their teeth, to devour, and to gore with their horns.
They even began to devour those cattle, and all the children of the earth began to shake and tremble before them and run away from them.

notes.text: A star: the first fallen angel, probably Asael (Azazel), compare 88:1 and 10:4.
The line of Seth (white) and the line of Cain (black) mingle.
The Watchers come down (chapter 6; Gen 6:1–4).
The giants, in three kinds, compare 7:2 and the note there.

verses.text: Again I saw how they began to gore one another and devour one another, and the earth began to cry out.
I raised my eyes to heaven again and saw in the vision beings coming out of heaven who looked like white men.{a} Four came out from that place, and three with them.

The three who came out last took me by the hand and carried me off, far from the earth’s generations, up to a lofty place. They showed me a tower rising high above the earth, with all the hills lower than it.
One of them said to me, “Stay here until you see everything that happens to those elephants, camels, and donkeys, and to the stars and the cattle, all of them.”

notes.text: Like white men: angels. The four are the archangels of chapter 10 (Michael, Gabriel, Raphael, and Sariel or Phanuel); the three with them are other angels who take Enoch up.

verses.text: I saw one of the four who had come out first seize that first star which had fallen from heaven. He tied it hand and foot and threw it into an abyss; that abyss was narrow and deep, dreadful and dark.{a}
Another of them unsheathed a sword and handed it to the elephants, camels, and donkeys, and they began to strike one another, and the whole earth shook because of them.{b}

As I watched in the vision, one of the four who had come out threw stones down from heaven, gathered and took all the great stars whose organs were like stallions’, tied them all hand and foot, and threw them into an abyss of the earth.

notes.text: Compare 10:4–5, where Raphael binds Asael and casts him into darkness.
Compare 10:9–12.

verses.text: One of those four went to that white bull{a} and taught him a secret, without his being afraid. He had been born a bull and became a man. He built himself a great vessel and lived on it, and three bulls lived with him in that vessel, and they were shut in.
Again I raised my eyes toward heaven and saw a high roof with seven streams of water on it, and those streams poured a great deal of water into an enclosure.
I looked again, and springs opened on the floor of that great enclosure, and the water began to swell and rise over the floor. I watched that enclosure until its whole floor was covered with water.
Water, darkness, and mist grew over it. When I looked at how high the water was, it had risen above the height of the enclosure and was pouring over it, and it stood on the earth.
All the cattle of that enclosure were herded together until I saw them sink, swallowed up, and die in that water.

But the vessel floated on the water, while all the cattle, elephants, camels, and donkeys sank to the bottom with all the animals. I could no longer see them; they could not get away, but died and sank into the depths.
Again I watched in the vision until those streams were taken away from that high roof, the chasms of the earth were leveled, and other abysses were opened.
Then the water began to drain into these until the earth could be seen. The vessel came to rest on the earth, the darkness withdrew, and light appeared.

That white bull who had become a man came out of the vessel, and the three bulls with him. One of the three was white like that bull, one was red as blood, and one was black. And that white bull left them.{b}

They began to produce wild animals and birds, so that there came to be different kinds: lions, leopards, wolves, dogs, hyenas, wild boars, foxes, badgers, pigs, falcons, vultures, kites, eagles, and ravens. Among them a white bull was born.{c}
They began to bite one another. But the white bull born among them fathered a wild donkey and a white bull with it, and the wild donkeys multiplied.{d}
The bull born from him fathered a black wild boar and a white sheep. The boar fathered many boars, but the sheep fathered twelve sheep.{e}
When those twelve sheep had grown, they handed one of them over to the donkeys, and the donkeys in turn handed that sheep over to the wolves, and that sheep grew up among the wolves.{f}
The Lord brought the other eleven to share its home and pasture among the wolves, and they increased into many flocks.

The wolves began to fear them and oppressed them, even destroying their little ones; they threw their young into a river full of water.{g} But the sheep began to cry out over their little ones and to complain to their Lord.

A sheep that had been rescued from the wolves fled and escaped to the wild donkeys.{h} I saw the sheep mourning and crying out, pleading with their Lord with all their strength, until the Lord of the sheep came down from a lofty dwelling at the sheep’s cry and came to them and shepherded them.
He called the sheep that had escaped the wolves and spoke with it about the wolves, that it should warn them not to touch the sheep.

The sheep went to the wolves as the Lord had said, and another sheep met it and went with it.{i} The two went together into the gathering of those wolves and spoke with them, warning them not to touch the sheep from then on.
After that I saw the wolves oppress the sheep harshly with all their might, and the sheep cried out.
The Lord came to the sheep, and they began to strike those wolves.{j} The wolves began to wail, but the sheep grew quiet and at once stopped crying out.
I watched the sheep until they left the wolves behind. But the wolves’ eyes were blinded, and they set out after the sheep with all their might.
The Lord of the sheep led the way, with his whole flock behind him. His face was dazzling, glorious, and fearful to look at.
But the wolves began to chase those sheep until they reached a sea of water.
That sea was split, and the water stood on one side and the other in front of them. Their Lord went at their head and stood between the flock and the wolves.{k}
Since the wolves did not yet see the sheep, they went into the middle of that sea; the wolves followed the sheep and ran after them into the sea.
When they saw the Lord of the sheep, they turned to run from his face, but the sea came back together and became as it had been made; the water swelled and rose until it covered those wolves.
I watched until all the wolves chasing those sheep had died and drowned.

The sheep, however, came safely out of the water into a desert without water or pasture, and there their eyes started to open so that they could see.{l} I saw the Lord of the sheep shepherding them, providing water and pasture, while that sheep went ahead as their guide.
That sheep went up to the top of that high rock,{m} and the Lord of the sheep sent it to them.
After that I saw the Lord of the sheep standing in front of them. His appearance was great, fearful, and majestic; all those sheep saw him and were afraid before his face.
They were all afraid and trembled because of him, and they cried out to the sheep that was with them, “We cannot stand before our Lord or look at him.”{n}
The sheep that led them went up again to the top of that rock. Meanwhile the flock grew blind and strayed from the path it had shown them, and that sheep did not know it.{o}
The Lord of the sheep was very angry with them. That sheep found out, came down from the top of the rock, came to the sheep, and found most of them blinded and gone astray.
When they saw it, they were afraid and trembled before it, and wanted to go back to their folds.

That sheep took other sheep with it, came to the sheep that had strayed, and began to kill them,{p} and the sheep were afraid of it. So that sheep brought back the strayed sheep, and they returned to their folds.
In this vision I kept watching until that sheep turned into a man, constructed a house for the Lord of the sheep, and settled the whole flock in it.{q}

I watched until the sheep that had met the sheep who led them fell asleep.{r} I watched until all the great sheep died and young ones took their place; these reached a pasture and drew near a stream.{s}
Then that sheep, their leader who had become a man, parted from them and fell asleep, and all the sheep looked for it and wept over it bitterly.{t}
I watched until they stopped weeping for that sheep and crossed that stream of water. Then two sheep arose as leaders in place of those who had led them and fallen asleep.{u}
I watched until the sheep came to a good place, a pleasant and glorious land, and I watched until those sheep were satisfied; and that house stood among them in the pleasant land.
Sometimes their eyes were opened and sometimes blinded, until another sheep rose up to lead them and turned them all back, and their eyes came open.{v}
The dogs, foxes, and wild boars began to devour those sheep, until the Lord of the sheep raised up a ram from among them to lead them.{w}
That ram began to butt those dogs, foxes, and wild boars on every side, until he had destroyed them all.
That sheep whose eyes were opened saw that ram among the sheep, until it abandoned its glory and began to butt those sheep, trample them, and behave disgracefully.
The Lord of the sheep sent the lamb to another lamb, to make it a ram and leader of the sheep in place of the ram that had abandoned its glory.{x}
It went to it, spoke with it privately, and made it a ram, prince and leader of the sheep; but through all this those dogs were oppressing the sheep.
The first ram chased that second ram, and the second ram got up and fled from it. I watched until those dogs brought down the first ram.{y}
The second ram then took the lead of the young sheep.

The flock increased greatly, while every dog, foxes, and wild boars were afraid and fled from it. The ram gored the wild beasts to death, and they had no more power among the sheep and robbed them of nothing. This ram had many offspring and then died, and a young sheep took its place as ram and became prince and leader of those sheep.{z}

That house became large and wide, and it was built for those sheep. On the house rose a great high tower for the Lord of the sheep.{aa} The house was low, but the tower was raised high, and the Lord of the sheep took his stand upon it, and a full table was laid before him.

Again I saw those sheep going astray and walking in many paths and abandoning that house of theirs. The Lord of the sheep summoned some of the flock and sent them to the rest, who set about killing them.{ab}

One of them was saved and not killed. It hurried away and cried out over the sheep, and they tried to kill it, but the Lord of the sheep rescued it from them, lifted it up to where I was, and settled it there.{ac}
He sent many other sheep to those sheep to testify to them and lament over them.

After that I saw that when they abandoned the house of the Lord and his tower, they fell away completely and their eyes were blinded. I saw the Lord of the sheep carry out great slaughter among them in their flocks, until those sheep brought on that slaughter themselves and betrayed his place.
He handed them over to the lions and leopards, the wolves and hyenas, the foxes, and all the wild beasts, and those wild beasts began to tear those sheep apart.
I saw that he abandoned that house of theirs and their tower and gave them all over to the lions to tear and devour them, to all the wild beasts.
I began to cry out with all my strength and appeal to the Lord of the sheep, pleading with him about the sheep, that they were being devoured by all the wild beasts.
But he stayed silent, though he saw it, and was glad that they were devoured, swallowed, and robbed, and left them to be devoured by all the beasts.

He called seventy shepherds{ad} and threw those sheep to them to pasture them. He said to the shepherds and their companions, “From now on, each of you is to pasture the sheep, and do everything I command you.
I will hand them over to you counted, and tell you which of them are to be destroyed; destroy those.” And he handed those sheep over to them.
He called another and said to him, “Watch and note everything the shepherds do to these sheep, for they will kill more of them than my orders allow.{ae}
Write down every excess and destruction the shepherds carry out: how many they destroy at my command and how many on their own whim. Record against each shepherd all the destruction he causes.

Read me the tally of those they kill and those they give up to be killed, so that it may stand as evidence against them and I may know all the shepherds’ actions and judge their conduct, whether they keep the command I gave them.
But they must not know it. Do not tell them or warn them, but simply record against each one all the destruction the shepherds cause, each in his time, and bring it all up to me.”
I watched until those shepherds pastured in their season, and they began to kill and destroy more than they had been told, and they handed those sheep over to the lions.
The lions and leopards ate and devoured most of those sheep, with the wild boars sharing the meal; and they burned that tower and tore down that house.{af}
I grieved deeply over that tower, because the house of the sheep had been torn down, and afterward I could not see whether those sheep went into that house.

The shepherds and their companions handed those sheep over to all the wild beasts to devour them, and each of them received a set number in his time. The other wrote in a book how many of them each one destroyed.
Each one killed and destroyed far more than was allotted, and I began to weep and mourn over those sheep.

So in the vision I saw the one who wrote: how he wrote down each one destroyed by those shepherds, day by day, and carried the whole book up, laid it down, and showed it to the Lord of the sheep—everything they had done, all that each of them had done away with, and all they had handed over to destruction.
It was read aloud to the Lord of the sheep; then he took it from the writer, read it himself, sealed it, and set it aside.

Right away I saw the shepherds pasture for twelve hours.{ag} Three of those sheep turned back, came and went in, and began to rebuild everything of that house that had fallen down;{ah} the wild boars tried to stop them but could not.{ai}

They began to build again as before, and they raised up that tower, and it was called the high tower. Once more they laid a table in front of the tower, yet every loaf on it was polluted and unclean.{aj}
Through all this the flock’s eyes were sightless, and so were their shepherds’. Great numbers were handed to the shepherds to be destroyed, who stamped on them and ate them up.
The Lord of the sheep stayed silent until all the sheep were scattered over the field and mixed with the beasts, and the shepherds did not rescue them from the beasts.

The one who wrote the book carried it up, showed it, and read it before the Lord of the sheep. He pleaded with him on their behalf and begged him for them as he showed him all the shepherds’ deeds, and he testified before him against all the shepherds.
He took the book itself, laid it down beside him, and left.

notes.text: That white bull: Noah. He is born a bull but becomes a man, perhaps meaning he is taught by angels or set apart; Moses likewise becomes a man in verse 36. The three bulls are Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
Shem is white (the chosen line); Ham and Japheth are red and black, though which is which is uncertain.

The wild animals and birds are the nations. Lions, leopards, and others appear later as Israel’s oppressors: Egyptians are wolves; Philistines dogs; Edomites wild boars; Ammonites and Moabites foxes; Assyrians lions; Babylonians leopards (or tigers); Greeks eagles and other birds of prey; Seleucid Syrians ravens. *A white bull*: Abraham.
A wild donkey: Ishmael, called “a wild donkey of a man” in Gen 16:12. *A white bull*: Isaac. The wild donkeys are the Arabs or Midianites.
The black wild boar: Esau, ancestor of Edom. *The white sheep*: Jacob, whose twelve sons are the twelve sheep. From here on Israel is pictured as sheep.
Joseph, sold to the Ishmaelites/Midianites and taken to Egypt (Gen 37:25–36).
Moses, who fled to Midian (Exod 2:15).
Another sheep: Aaron (Exod 4:27).
The plagues of Egypt (Exod 7–12).
Opening and blinding of the eyes is the vision’s image for Israel’s faithfulness and apostasy.
Mount Sinai (Exod 19).
The golden calf (Exod 32).
The Levites’ slaughter in Exod 32:26–28.
