The house: here the tabernacle (Exod 25–40); later it stands for Jerusalem, with the “tower” as the temple.
Fell asleep: died. Aaron’s death (Num 20:28).
The Jordan.
The death of Moses (Deut 34).
Two sheep: perhaps Joshua and Caleb, or Joshua and Eleazar.
The period of the judges; the other sheep is probably Samuel.
A ram: Saul, the first king. The dogs are the Philistines; the foxes Ammon and Moab; the boars Edom/Amalek.
The lamb sent is Samuel; the other lamb is David (1 Sam 16).
Saul pursues David and dies fighting the Philistines (1 Sam 18–31).
The last sentence (Charles’s 48b) tells of David’s death and Solomon’s succession; some manuscripts place it after verse 48.
The tower: Solomon’s temple. The house is now Jerusalem.
The prophets, compare 1 Kgs 19:10; Neh 9:26.
Elijah, taken up to heaven (2 Kgs 2:11), now dwelling with Enoch.

Seventy shepherds: angelic rulers set over Israel from the exile to the end time, each for a fixed period. The number recalls the seventy years of Jer 25:11–12 and the seventy weeks of years of Dan 9:24, and the seventy nations of Gen 10. Their periods fall into four groups of 12, 23, 23, and 12 (89:72; 90:1, 5).
Another: a recording angel, perhaps Michael (compare 90:14, 17).
The Babylonian destruction of Jerusalem and the temple in 587/586 BC, with Edom joining in (Obad 10–14; Ps 137:7).
Twelve hours: the periods of twelve shepherds, the Persian era. Each shepherd’s term is called an hour.
Three sheep: probably Zerubbabel, Jeshua the high priest, and Ezra or Nehemiah (Ezra 3–6; Neh 2–6).
The wild boars: here the Samaritans and neighboring peoples who opposed the rebuilding (Ezra 4).
The author judges the worship of the second temple to be impure, perhaps over calendar or priestly disputes; compare Mal 1:7.

verses.text: I watched until thirty-five shepherds had taken up the pasturing in this way,{a} each completing his term as the first ones had; and others took them in hand to pasture them for their term, each shepherd in his own term.

Next in my vision every bird of the air came flocking: eagles, vultures, kites, and ravens, with the eagles at the head of them all,{b} and they set upon the sheep, pecking out their eyes and feeding on their flesh.
The sheep cried out because the birds were eating their flesh. As for me, I looked on and mourned in my sleep over that shepherd who was pasturing the sheep.

I watched until those sheep were devoured by the dogs, eagles, and kites, and they left them no flesh, skin, or sinew, until only their bones were standing; then their bones too fell to the ground, and the sheep became few.
I watched until twenty-three had taken up the pasturing and completed, in their terms, fifty-eight periods.{c}
But look: lambs were born to those white sheep,{d} and they began to open their eyes and see, and to cry out to the sheep.
They cried out to them, but the sheep did not listen to what they said; they were completely deaf, and their eyes were utterly blinded.
I saw in the vision the ravens swoop on those lambs and seize one of them,{e} and tear the sheep to pieces and devour them.
I watched until horns grew on those lambs, and the ravens knocked their horns down. Then I watched until a great horn sprouted on one of those sheep,{f} and their eyes were opened.
It looked at them, and it cried out to the sheep, and the rams caught sight of it and came running to it together.
Still, through all this, those eagles, vultures, ravens, and kites kept tearing the sheep, swooping on them and devouring them. The sheep stayed silent, but the rams mourned and cried out.
The ravens fought hard against it, striving to topple its horn, yet they could not prevail.

I watched until the shepherds, eagles, vultures, and kites came and called to the ravens to break the horn of that ram. They fought and battled with it, and it fought with them and cried out for its help to come.{g}
I kept watching until the man who listed the shepherds’ names and took them up to the Lord of the sheep arrived to aid it and revealed all things to it; he had descended to assist that ram.{h}
I watched until the Lord of the sheep came to them in anger, and everyone who saw him ran, and all of them collapsed into his shadow away from his presence.
All the eagles, vultures, ravens, and kites gathered together, and all the sheep of the field came with them; they all came together and helped one another to break that ram’s horn.{i}

I watched that man who wrote the book at the Lord’s command, until he opened the book about the destruction that the last twelve shepherds had done, and showed before the Lord of the sheep that they had destroyed far more than those before them.

I watched until the Lord of the sheep came to them, took in his hand the staff of his anger, and struck the earth. The earth split open, and all the beasts and all the birds of the sky fell away from those sheep and were swallowed up in the earth, and it closed over them.
I kept watching until the sheep were handed a mighty sword and marched out against all the beasts of the field to kill them, and all the beasts and birds of the sky fled from before them.
I watched until a throne was set up in the pleasant land,{j} and the Lord of the sheep sat on it, and the other took the sealed books and opened them before the Lord of the sheep.{k}

The Lord called those men, the first seven white ones,{l} and ordered them to bring before him all the stars whose organs were like stallions’, starting with the first star that led the way; and they brought them all before him.

He said to the man who wrote before him, who was one of those seven white ones, “Take those seventy shepherds to whom I handed over the sheep, and who on their own authority took them and killed more than I commanded.”
And look, I saw them all bound, and they all stood before him.
Judgment was held first on the stars. Tried and convicted, they were sent off to the place of sentence; they were thrown into an abyss full of fire and flame and full of pillars of fire.{m}
The seventy shepherds were then tried, convicted, and hurled into that abyss of fire.

At that time I saw a similar abyss opened in the middle of the earth, full of fire. The blinded sheep were led in, every one tried and convicted, and cast into this blazing pit, where they burned. It lay on the right-hand side of the house.{n}
I watched the sheep burn, bones and all.

I stood up to look, until they folded up that old house. They carried off all its pillars, and all the beams and decorations of the house were folded up with it, and they carried it away and put it in a place in the south of the land.

I kept watching until the Lord of the sheep brought in a fresh house, bigger and loftier than before, and raised it where the folded-up one had stood. Every pillar in it was new, and its adornments were new too, and grander than those of the old house he had removed. All the sheep were inside it.{o}
I saw every remaining sheep, with every beast of the earth and every bird of the air, bowing down and paying homage to those sheep, pleading with them and obeying them in everything.{p}

After that, those three who were dressed in white, who had taken me by the hand and brought me up before, took me up with the hand of that ram also holding me, and set me down among those sheep before the judgment took place.{q}
Every one of those sheep was white, with fleece thick and clean.

All that had been destroyed and scattered, along with every wild beast and every bird of the air, assembled in the house, and the Lord of the sheep was full of joy because they were all good and had come back to his house.

I watched until they laid down that sword that had been given to the sheep; they brought it back into the house, and it was sealed in the Lord’s presence. All the sheep were invited into that house, but it could not hold them.
Every one of them had open eyes and beheld what was good, and there was not one among them who did not see.
I saw that the house was large and wide and very full.
Then I saw a white bull born, big-horned,{r} and every wild beast and every bird of the air stood in awe of him and made constant petition to him.

I watched until all their kinds were transformed and they all became white bulls. The first among them became a lamb,{s} which grew into a mighty creature with huge black horns on its head; and the Lord of the sheep took delight in it and in the whole herd.
I slept among them, and I woke up having seen everything.
This is the vision I saw while I slept. I woke up and blessed the Lord of righteousness and gave him glory.

Then I wept bitterly, and my tears would not stop until I could bear it no longer. When I looked, they ran down because of what I had seen, for everything will come and be fulfilled, and all human deeds in their order were shown to me.
On that same night the earlier dream came back to me, and it made me weep and left me shaken, for I had seen that vision.”

notes.text: Thirty-five shepherds: 12 of the Persian period plus 23 more, carrying the story into the Greek period after Alexander the Great (332 BC).
The eagles: the Macedonians/Greeks, probably the Ptolemies of Egypt, who ruled Judea about 301–200 BC. The ravens are the Seleucids of Syria.
Fifty-eight periods: 12 + 23 + 23 shepherds, leaving the last 12 for the final age (90:17).
The lambs: a reform movement among pious Jews in the early second century BC, perhaps the group behind this book or the Hasidim of 1 Macc 2:42.
One of those lambs: probably the high priest Onias III, murdered about 171 BC (2 Macc 4:33–35; compare Dan 9:26).

A great horn: Judas Maccabeus, leader of the Jewish revolt against the Seleucid king Antiochus IV from 166 BC (1 Macc 3–9). The vision’s history ends with his struggles, which dates it to about 164–160 BC.
Verses 13–15 and 16–18 seem to be two versions of the same scene; Charles rearranged them (13, 16, 19 then 14, 15, 17, 18). This translation keeps the manuscript order.
That man: the recording angel of 89:61, often taken as Michael, who in 2 Macc 11:6–8 sends a heavenly rider to aid Judas.
The sheep of the field: probably wild sheep, that is, the Hellenizing Jews who sided with the Seleucids.
The pleasant land: the land of Israel (compare Dan 8:9; 11:16).
Compare Dan 7:9–10.
The first seven white ones: the seven archangels (20:1–8; compare 87:2).
To the right: south of Jerusalem, the Valley of Hinnom (Gehenna); compare 27:1–3.
The new house: a new Jerusalem built by God himself; compare Isa 54:11–12; Ezek 40–48; Rev 21:2. Notably no tower (temple) is mentioned.
Compare Isa 49:23; 60:14.
Before the judgment: the order is odd; some read “before the judgment” as “after.” The ram may be Elijah, here pictured as a ram, who returns before the end (Mal 4:5); compare 89:52.
A white bull: a messianic figure. Humanity returns to the condition of Adam (the first white bull, 85:3), and all the nations become white bulls.

A lamb: the Ethiopic word *nagar* (“word,” or a corruption) is unclear; Charles emended to “wild ox” (Hebrew *reʾem*), others keep “lamb.” This translation follows the common reading “lamb,” noting the uncertainty.

verses.text: Then Methuselah went and called all his brothers to him and gathered his relatives.

He spoke to all the children of righteousness and said,
“Hear, you sons of Enoch, all your father’s words,
and listen well to the voice of my mouth.
I urge you and tell you, beloved:
love uprightness and walk in it.

Do not come near uprightness with a divided heart,
and do not keep company with the double-hearted,
but walk in righteousness, my sons.
It will guide you on good paths,
and righteousness will go with you.

Wrongdoing will again reach its full measure on the earth,
and all deeds of wrongdoing, violence,
and transgression will prevail twice over.

When sin, wrongdoing, blasphemy,
and violence in every kind of deed increase,
and apostasy, transgression, and impurity increase,
a great punishment will come from heaven on all these,
and the holy Lord will come out in anger and punishment
to carry out judgment on the earth.

In those days violence will be cut off at its roots,
and the roots of wrongdoing together with deceit,
and they will be destroyed from under heaven.

All the idols of the nations will be given up,
their temples burned with fire,
and they will be removed from the whole earth.
The nations will be thrown into the judgment of fire
and perish in anger and in harsh judgment forever.

The righteous will rise from their sleep,
and wisdom will rise and be given to them.

After that the roots of wrongdoing will be cut off, and the sinners will be destroyed by the sword … will be severed from the blasphemers everywhere; schemers of violence and speakers of blasphemy alike will fall by the sword.{c}

After that there will be another week, the eighth, the week of righteousness,{d}
and a sword will be given to it,
so that righteous judgment may be carried out on the oppressors,
and sinners will be handed over to the righteous.

At its end they will gain houses through their righteousness,
and a house will be built for the Great King in glory forever.{e}

After that, in the ninth week,
righteous judgment will be revealed to the whole world;
all the works of the wicked will vanish from the whole earth,
the world will be written down for destruction,
and all humankind will look to the path of uprightness.

After this, in the tenth week, in its seventh part,
there will be the great eternal judgment,
in which he will take vengeance among the angels.

After that there will be many weeks without number, forever,
in goodness and righteousness,
and sin will never again be mentioned.

So now, my sons, I am telling you and pointing out to you
which roads lead to righteousness and which to violence.
I will show them to you again,
so that you may know what will happen.

Listen to me now, my sons:
keep to the roads of righteousness
and keep off the roads of violence;
for everyone who travels the roads of wrongdoing will perish forever.”

notes.text: Chapters 91–108 make up the final section of 1 Enoch: Enoch’s instruction to his children (91), the Apocalypse of Weeks (93:1–10 with 91:11–17), and the Epistle proper (92; 94–105), followed by the Birth of Noah (106–107) and a closing appendix (108). The Aramaic fragments (4QEn g) and the Greek Chester Beatty papyrus (for 97:6–107:3) are reported to support most of it; it is usually dated to the second century BC. In the Ethiopic manuscripts the order is disturbed: the last three “weeks” (91:12–17) stand before the first seven (93:3–10). The Aramaic is reported to have them in sequence, and many translations rearrange them; this translation keeps the Ethiopic order and numbering, and the notes point to the sequence.
The first end: the flood.
The text of this verse is damaged; the gap is marked by an ellipsis.

The eighth week: in the sequence of the Apocalypse of Weeks this follows 93:10. Each “week” is an age of world history; the author probably lived in the seventh, the time of the “apostate generation” (93:9) in the early second century BC.
A house … for the Great King: a new temple. *The Great King*: God (compare Ps 48:2; Matt 5:35).
Compare Isa 65:17; 66:22; 2 Pet 3:13; Rev 21:1.

verses.text: The book written by Enoch—Enoch wrote this complete teaching of wisdom, praised by everyone and judge of the whole earth—for every child of mine who will dwell on the earth, and for the generations to come who will practice uprightness and peace.{a}

Do not let your spirit be troubled because of the times,
for the Holy and Great One has set days for everything.

He will be gracious to the righteous one and give him lasting uprightness,
and give him power, so that he will have goodness and righteousness
and walk in eternal light.

Sin will perish in darkness forever
and will not be seen again from that day on, forever.

notes.text: This verse is the heading of the Epistle of Enoch proper; the bracketed words in Charles (“Enoch indeed wrote … all the earth”) may be a scribe’s addition.

verses.text: Afterward Enoch handed on the books and began to tell from them.

Enoch said,
“About the children of righteousness,
about the chosen of the world,
and about the plant of uprightness,{a} I will speak these things;
I, Enoch, will declare them to you, my sons,
according to what appeared to me in the heavenly vision,
what I learned from the word of the holy angels,
and what I came to understand from the heavenly tablets.”

After me, in the second week, great wickedness will arise,
and deceit will have sprung up.
In it will be the first end,{c}
and in it a man will be saved.
After it is over, wrongdoing will grow,
and a law will be made for the sinners.

After that, at the end of the fifth week,
the house of glory and dominion will be built forever.{f}

After that, in the sixth week, all who live in it will be blinded,
and the hearts of all of them will godlessly abandon wisdom.
In it a man will go up,{g}
and at its end the house of dominion will be burned with fire,
and the whole race of the chosen root will be scattered.
For who is there among all humankind who can hear the voice of the Holy One without being shaken? Who can think his thoughts? Who is there who can look on all the works of heaven?{i}
How could anyone look at heaven? Who could grasp heavenly things, or see a soul or spirit and report on it, or go up and see all their ends and grasp them or act like them?
Who among all people could know how wide and how long the earth is, and to whom has the measure of all of them been shown?
Or is there anyone who could tell the length of heaven, how great its height is, what it rests on, how many stars there are, and where all the lights rest?

notes.text: The plant of uprightness (or righteousness): Israel, or the faithful within it; compare 10:16; 84:6; Isa 60:21; 61:3.
The seventh: Enoch is the seventh from Adam (Gen 5; Jude 14).
The first end: the flood. *A man*: Noah. *A law … for the sinners*: the laws given after the flood (Gen 9:1–7).
A man: Abraham. His descendants, Israel, are “the plant of righteousness.”
The law of Sinai and the tabernacle (or the land of Israel as an “enclosure”).
The temple of Solomon.
A man: Elijah (2 Kgs 2:11). *The house of dominion … burned*: the destruction of the temple in 587/586 BC and the exile.
The sequence continues at 91:11–17 (weeks eight to ten).
Verses 11–14 are a separate wisdom poem on the limits of human knowledge, compare Job 38; Isa 40:12–14; Sir 1:2–3. Its rhetorical questions contrast with Enoch, who has been shown these things.

verses.text:
To certain people of a generation the paths of violence and of death will be revealed,
and they will keep far from them
and not follow them.

Now I tell you, the righteous:
do not walk in the path of evil or in the paths of death,
and do not come near them, so that you are not destroyed.

But seek and choose for yourselves righteousness and a chosen life,
and walk in the paths of peace,
and you will live and prosper.

Woe to those who build their houses with sin;
for they will be overthrown from all their foundations
and fall by the sword.
Those who get gold and silver in judgment will suddenly perish.

You have committed blasphemy and wrongdoing
and have made yourselves ready for the day of slaughter,
the day of darkness and the day of the great judgment.

So I tell you and declare to you:
the one who created you will overthrow you,
and there will be no pity at your fall,
and your Creator will rejoice at your destruction.

In those days your righteous ones will be
a rebuke to the sinners and the wicked.

notes.text: The woes (94:6–100:9; 103:5–8) attack wealthy oppressors and apostates, in the style of the prophets (Isa 5:8–23; Amos 6:1–7) and of Luke 6:24–26.

verses.text:
If only my eyes were a cloud of water,
so that I might weep over you
and pour down my tears like rain from a cloud,
and so find rest from my heart’s distress!

Who has allowed you to practice insult and wickedness?
Judgment will catch up with you, sinners.

Woe to you who pronounce curses that cannot be undone;
healing will be far from you because of your sins.

Woe to you who repay your neighbor with evil;
for you will be repaid according to your deeds.

Woe to you, lying witnesses,
and those who weigh out injustice,
for you will suddenly perish.

Take hope, you righteous! For the sinners will suddenly perish before you,
and you will rule over them as you wish.

Woe to you, sinners, for your riches make you look like the righteous,
yet your own hearts expose you as sinners,
and that will testify against you, a reminder of your evil deeds.

Woe to you, the mighty,
who use your might to oppress the righteous;
for your day of ruin is on its way.
Then many good days will come to the righteous, on the day of your judgment.

notes.text: Rock badgers: the hyrax, a small animal that shelters in rocks (Ps 104:18; Prov 30:26). *The sirens*: the Ethiopic borrows the Greek *seirēnes*, which the Greek Bible uses for desert creatures (perhaps ostriches or jackals) in Isa 13:21. The verse is obscure and some think it is out of place.
Compare Amos 6:6.
Compare Jer 2:13.

verses.text:
Believe, you righteous, that the sinners will be put to shame
and perish on the day of wrongdoing.

Know, you sinners, that the Most High has your destruction in mind,
and the angels of heaven rejoice over your destruction.

What will you do, you sinners,
and where will you run on that day of judgment,
when you hear the sound of the prayer of the righteous?

You will fare like those
against whom this word will stand as evidence:
“You have been companions of sinners.”

At that time the righteous will pray and be heard by the Lord,
and your time of judgment will arrive.

Woe to you, sinners, who live in the middle of the sea and on the dry land;
the memory of you is evil against you.

Woe to you who get silver and gold unjustly and say,
“We have grown rich and have possessions,
and have gotten everything we wanted.

Your lies will flow away like water,
for your wealth will not last
but will quickly fly up from you;
because you got it all unjustly,
you will be handed over to a great curse.

notes.text: From 97:6 to 107:3 a Greek text survives in the Chester Beatty–Michigan papyrus (fourth century AD). Where it differs from the Ethiopic in meaning, the notes say so.
Compare Luke 12:16–21.

verses.text:
Now I swear to you, the wise and the foolish,
that you will see many things on the earth.

You men will put on more finery than a woman
and more colors than a young girl;
in royalty, grandeur, and power,
in silver, gold, and purple,
in splendor and in food you will be poured out like water.

So they will lack teaching and wisdom,
and through this they will perish along with their possessions;
with all their glory and splendor,
in shame, slaughter, and great poverty,
their spirits will be thrown into the furnace of fire.

Barrenness was not given to woman;
because of the deeds of her own hands she dies childless.{b}

By the Holy Great One I swear to you, sinners,
that every evil thing you do lies open in heaven,
and none of your oppressive deeds are covered or hidden.
Do not think in your spirit or say in your heart that you do not know and do not see that every sin is recorded every day in heaven before the Most High.
From now on you know that all the oppression you inflict is written down every day until the day of your judgment.
Woe to you, fools, for you will perish through your folly. You sin against the wise, and so good fortune will not be your share.

Now know that you are ready for the day of destruction. Do not hope to live, sinners; you will go away and die, for you know no ransom. You are made ready for the day of the great judgment, for the day of distress and great shame for your spirits.

Woe to you, stubborn of heart, who do evil and eat blood!{c} Where do you get good things to eat and drink and be full? From all the good things the Lord Most High has placed in abundance on the earth. So you will have no peace.

Woe to you who love deeds of wrongdoing! Why do you hope for good fortune for yourselves? Know that you will be handed over to the righteous, and they will cut off your necks and kill you and show you no mercy.
Woe to you who rejoice at the distress of the righteous, for no grave will be dug for you.
Woe to you who treat the words of the righteous as nothing, for you will have no hope of life.
Woe to you who write down lying and wicked words; for they write down their lies so that people will hear them and act wickedly toward their neighbor.{d}
So they will have no peace but will die a sudden death.

notes.text: Sin was not sent: the Epistle insists on human responsibility for sin, in tension with the Book of the Watchers, which traces evil to the fallen angels (chapters 6–16).
The meaning is uncertain; the sense may be that suffering comes from human deeds, not from God’s decree.
Eat blood: forbidden in Gen 9:4; Lev 17:10–14.
Perhaps aimed at rival teachers or writings; compare 104:10–11.

verses.text:
Woe to those who twist the words of uprightness
and break the eternal law,
and make themselves into what they were not, into sinners;
they will be trampled on the earth.

In those days, you righteous, get ready to raise your prayers as a reminder
and set them as evidence before the angels,
so that they may set the sin of the sinners as a reminder before the Most High.

In those days the nations will be stirred up,
and the families of the nations will rise on the day of destruction.

In those days the destitute will go out and carry off their children
and abandon them, so that their children perish because of them;
they will abandon their nursing infants and not return to them,
and will have no pity on their loved ones.
Again I swear to you, sinners, that sin is made ready for a day of unending bloodshed.

Those who worship stones, and carved images of gold, silver, wood, stone, and clay, and those who worship unclean spirits and demons and all kinds of idols in ignorance, will get no help at all from them.

They will become wicked through the folly of their hearts,
and their eyes will be blinded by the fear of their hearts
and by visions in their dreams.

Through these they will become wicked and afraid,
for they will have done all their work in a lie
and worshiped a stone;
so in an instant they will perish.

But in those days, happy is everyone who takes wisdom’s words to heart and grasps them,
who keeps to the Most High’s ways and follows his righteous road,
and do not become wicked with the wicked;
for they will be saved.

Woe to you who spread evil to your neighbors;
for you will be killed in Sheol.{a}

Woe to those who do wrong and help oppression,
and kill their neighbors, until the day of the great judgment.

For he will throw down your glory,
bring affliction on your hearts,
rouse his fierce anger,
and put every one of you to the sword;
and the holy and righteous, all of them, will recall your sins.

notes.text: *Sheol*: Hebrew *sheʾol*, the realm of the dead; compare 22:1–14.

verses.text:
In those days fathers will be struck down together with their sons in one place,
and brothers will fall dead one with another,
until the streams run with their blood.

The horse will wade up to its chest in the blood of sinners,
and the chariot will sink to its top.{a}

In those days the angels will come down into the hidden places
and gather in one place all who brought down sin,
and the Most High will rise on that day of judgment
to carry out great judgment among sinners.

Then the children of the earth will see the wise in safety
and grasp everything this book says,
and realize that wealth cannot save them
when their sins bring them down.

Woe to you, stubborn of heart,
who stay awake to plan wickedness;
fear will come on you,
and there will be no one to help you.
Now know that he will ask the angels in heaven about your deeds, and the sun, the moon, and the stars about your sins, because on the earth you pass judgment on the righteous.
He will call every cloud, mist, dew, and rain to testify against you; for they will all be held back because of you from coming down on you, and they will remember your sins.
Now go ahead and give gifts to the rain so that it will not be held back from coming down on you, or to the dew, if it has accepted gold and silver from you to come down!{c}
When frost and snow with their cold, and all the snowstorms with all their plagues, fall on you, in those days you will not be able to stand before them.

notes.text: Compare Rev 14:20.
Like the pupil of an eye: traditionally “the apple of the eye”; compare Deut 32:10; Ps 17:8.
Irony: the rich cannot bribe the weather. The Greek is reported to differ here.

verses.text: Look at the sky, you children of heaven, and at every work of the Most High; fear him and do no evil in his presence.
If he shuts the windows of heaven and holds back the rain and the dew from falling on the earth because of you, what will you do then?
If he sends his anger on you because of your deeds, you cannot plead with him, for you spoke proud and arrogant words against his righteousness. So you will have no peace.
Do you not see the sailors on ships, how their vessels are tossed about by the waves and shaken by the winds, and are in great danger?
They are afraid because all their valuable goods go out on the sea with them, and their hearts dread that the sea will swallow them and they will die in it.
Are not the whole sea and all its waters and all its motion the work of the Most High? Has he not set limits to what it does and hemmed it in on every side with sand?{a}
When he rebukes it, it takes fright and dries up, and every fish in it perishes, together with all that it holds. Yet you sinners who live on the land have no fear of him.
Is it not he who formed heaven and earth and whatever fills them? Who gave insight and wisdom to every creature that moves over the land and through the sea?
Do not the sailors fear the sea? Yet sinners do not fear the Most High.

notes.text: Compare Job 38:8–11; Jer 5:22.

verses.text:
In those days, when he brings a terrible fire on you,
where will you run, and where will you find rescue?
When he hurls his word against you,
will you not be shaken and afraid?

All the lights will be shaken with great fear,
and all the earth will be shaken and tremble in alarm.

All the angels will carry out their orders
and try to hide from the presence of the Great Glory,
and the children of the earth will tremble and shake.
You sinners will be cursed forever,
and you will have no peace.

Do not be afraid, you souls of the righteous;
take hope, you who have died in righteousness.

Do not grieve if your soul has gone down to Sheol in grief,
and your body did not fare in life as your goodness deserved;
but wait for the day of the sinners’ judgment,
the day of cursing and punishment.

Yet when you die, the sinners say over you,
“As we die, so the righteous die,
and what good have they gained from their deeds?
I tell you, sinners: you are content to eat and drink, to rob and sin, to strip people naked, to get wealth and see good days.
Have you seen how the righteous end, that no violence of any kind is found in them until they die?
“Still, they perished and became as though they had never been, and their spirits went down to Sheol in distress.”

notes.text: The sinners’ argument recalls Eccl 2:14–16; 3:19–21; Wis 2:1–5.

verses.text: And now I make this vow to you, the righteous, by the splendor of the Great One, the Honored and Powerful, who rules, and by his majesty I vow it to you:

I know a mystery;
I have read the heavenly tablets
and seen the holy books,
and I have found written and engraved in them about them:

every blessing, joy and glory has been made ready for them
and recorded for the spirits of those who have died in righteousness;
your reward for your hard work will be a rich share of good things,
and your portion is far better than the portion of those still alive.

The spirits of you who have died in righteousness will live and rejoice;
their spirits will not perish, nor their memory before the face of the Great One,
for all the generations of the world.
So do not fear their scorn any longer.

Woe to you, sinners, when you have died,
if you die in the wealth of your sins,
and those like you say of you,
“Happy are the sinners! They have seen all their days.

Now they have died in prosperity and wealth,
and have seen no distress or killing in their life;
they have died in honor,
and no judgment was carried out on them while they lived.”

Know that their souls will be brought down to Sheol,
and they will be wretched in their great distress.

Do not say of the righteous and good who are alive,
“In our troubled days we have worked hard and known every trouble;
we have met much evil and been worn out,
and have become few and small in spirit.

We were ruined, and nobody came to our aid, not even with a word;
we were tormented and crushed, and we gave up expecting to see another day of life.

Those who hated us and struck us have ruled over us,
and we bowed our necks to those who hated us,
but they had no pity on us.

We wanted to get away from them, to escape and rest,
but found no place to run to and be safe from them.

We complained to the rulers in our distress
and cried out against those who devoured us,
but they paid no attention to our cries
and would not listen to our voice.

They helped those who robbed us, devoured us, and made us few. They hid their oppression and did not remove from us the yoke of those who devoured us, scattered us, and murdered us. They hid their murders and did not remember that they had raised their hands against us.”{b}

notes.text: Compare Deut 28:13, 44.
Verses 9–15 voice the complaint of the righteous; the answer follows in chapter 104.

verses.text: I vow to you that the angels in heaven keep you in mind for good in the presence of the Great One’s glory, and that your names are inscribed there before him.{a}{a}

Take hope! For before, you were put to shame through evil and affliction, but now you will shine like the lights of heaven; you will shine and be seen, and the gates of heaven will be opened to you.{b}
When you cry out, let your cry be for justice, and justice will show itself to you; for all you have suffered will be avenged upon the rulers and upon everyone who aided your plunderers.
Take hope, and do not throw away your hope; for you will have great joy like the angels of heaven.

What will you have to do? You will not have to hide on the day of the great judgment, you will not be found as sinners, and the eternal judgment will be far from you for all the generations of the world.

Now do not be afraid, you righteous, when you see the sinners growing strong and prospering in their ways. Do not keep company with them, but keep far from their violence; for you will become companions of the hosts of heaven.
Though you sinners say, “None of our sins will be searched out and written down,” still they will write down all your sins every day.
Now I tell you that light and darkness, day and night, both look upon all your sins.

Do not be wicked in your hearts; do not lie or alter the words of uprightness, or call the words of the Holy Great One lies, or pay attention to your idols; for all your lying and all your wickedness lead not to righteousness but to great sin.
Now I know this mystery: sinners will alter and twist the words of righteousness in many ways; they will speak wicked words, lie, practice great deceptions, and write books about their own words.
But if they copy out my words faithfully into their own languages, neither altering them nor cutting anything away, but setting down faithfully everything that I first declared about them,{c}{c}
then I know another mystery: books will be given to the righteous and the wise, to be a source of joy, uprightness, and much wisdom.
The books will be given to them, and they will believe them and rejoice over them; and then all the righteous who have learned from them all the paths of uprightness will be rewarded.

notes.text: Compare Dan 12:1; Luke 10:20.
Compare Dan 12:3.
This passage, with its concern for faithful copying and translation “in their languages,” is notable in a work that itself survives mainly in translation. Compare Rev 22:18–19.

verses.text: In those days, says the Lord, they will call to the children of the earth and testify about their wisdom: “Show it to them, for you are their guides, and rewards over the whole earth.
For I and my son will be joined with them forever in the paths of uprightness in their lives. You will have peace. Rejoice, you children of uprightness!” Amen.{a}

notes.text: I and my son: the phrase is unusual; it may refer to God and the righteous (or Israel) as his son, or be a Christian touch. The Greek papyrus is reported to lack this chapter.

verses.text: Some days later my son Methuselah chose a wife for his son Lamech, and she conceived and bore him a son.{a}{a}

The child’s body was as white as snow and as ruddy as a rose in blossom; the hair on his head and his long locks were white like wool, and his eyes were lovely. When he opened his eyes, the whole house filled with light, as if the sun were shining in it.
Then he stood up in the hands of the midwife, opened his mouth, and spoke with the Lord of righteousness.
Lamech, his father, was terrified of him and ran away to his own father, Methuselah.

He said to him, “I have fathered a strange son, different from and unlike a human being, resembling the children of the God of heaven. His nature is different; he is not like us. His eyes are like the rays of the sun, and his face is glorious.
I think he cannot have come from me, but from the angels, and I fear that something extraordinary will happen on earth in his time.
Now, my father, I am here to plead with you and beg you to go to Enoch, our father, and learn the truth from him, for he lives among the angels.”

When Methuselah heard what his son said, he traveled to the ends of the earth to find me, for he had been told that I was there. He called out, and I heard his voice and went to him. I said to him, “I am here, my son. Why have you come to me?”
He answered, “I have come to you because of something that worries me greatly, a troubling sight.

Now, my father, hear me. A son has been born to my son Lamech, unlike anyone else. His nature is not like a human nature. The color of his body is whiter than snow and redder than a rose in bloom, the hair of his head is whiter than white wool, his eyes are like the rays of the sun, and when he opened his eyes he lit up the whole house.
He rose up from the midwife’s hands, opened his mouth, and praised the Lord of heaven.

His father Lamech became afraid and fled to me. He does not believe that the boy is his, but that he is in the likeness of the angels of heaven. So I have come to you so that you may tell me the truth.”

I, Enoch, replied, “The Lord is going to do something new on earth. I have seen it before in a vision, and I am telling you now: in the days of my father Jared, certain angels of heaven disobeyed the Lord’s command.{b}{b}
They sin and break the law; they have joined themselves to women and sin with them, have married some of them, and have fathered children by them.
A great destruction will come over the whole earth; there will be a flood and great destruction for one year.{c}
This son who has been born to you will be left on the earth, and his three children will be saved with him; when all humankind on the earth dies, he and his sons will be saved.
They will produce giants on the earth, not of spirit but of flesh, and there will be great punishment on the earth, and the earth will be cleansed of all impurity.{d}

Now tell your son Lamech that the one who has been born is truly his son. Name him Noah, for he will be left to you, and he and his sons will be saved from the destruction that will come on the earth because of all the sin and all the wrongdoing that will reach its full measure on the earth in his days.{e}

After that, injustice will grow greater still than the injustice that had at first reached its full measure on earth. For I know the mysteries of the holy ones: the Lord himself has revealed them to me and explained them, and I have read them on the heavenly tablets.

notes.text: Chapters 106–107 tell of Noah’s miraculous birth, a story also found in the Genesis Apocryphon from Qumran (1QapGen 2–5). *Lamech*: Hebrew *Lemekh*, of uncertain meaning (Gen 5:25–31).
*Jared*: Hebrew *Yered*, “descent,” explained in 6:6 as the time when the Watchers came down.
For one year: the flood lasts a year and ten days in Gen 7:11; 8:14 (or a full year by the 364-day calendar).
Charles moves verse 17 before 15 for sense; this translation keeps the usual numbering.
*Noah*: Hebrew *Noaḥ*, linked with *nuaḥ*, “rest,” and *niḥam*, “comfort” (Gen 5:29); compare 107:3.

verses.text: I saw written on them that generation after generation will do wrong, until a generation of righteousness arises, wrongdoing is destroyed, sin passes away from the earth, and every kind of good comes on it.
Now, my son, go and tell your son Lamech that this son who has been born is truly his son, and that this is no lie.”

When Methuselah heard the words of his father Enoch—for Enoch had disclosed everything to him in secret—he went back and reported them to Lamech, and the boy was named Noah, because he will bring comfort to the earth after all that destruction.
This is another book that Enoch wrote for his son Methuselah, and for those who come after him and keep the law in the final days.{a}{a}
You who have done good, wait for those days, until an end is made of those who do evil and of the power of the lawbreakers.

Wait until sin has passed away, for their names will be erased from the book of life and from the holy books; their offspring will be destroyed forever, and their spirits will be killed. They will cry out and mourn in a place that is a formless wasteland, and they will burn in the fire, for there is no earth there.{b}

There I saw a kind of cloud that I could not see through; it was so deep that I could not see over it. I saw a flame blazing brightly, and shining mountainlike shapes that wheeled and swung back and forth.
I asked one of the holy angels who accompanied me, “What is this glowing thing? It is no heaven, only the flame of a blazing fire, with a sound of weeping and crying, of lament and fierce pain.”

He said to me, “This place you see is where the spirits of sinners and blasphemers are thrown, and of those who do evil, and of those who twist everything the Lord has spoken through the mouth of the prophets about the things to come.

Some of these matters are written and engraved up in heaven, so that the angels can read them and learn what lies ahead for the sinners, and for the spirits of the humble, and for those who mortified their bodies and were repaid by God, and for those who were shamed by wicked people:
those who loved God, and cared nothing for gold or silver or any of the good things of the world, but surrendered their bodies to torture;

who from the time they came into being did not crave earthly food, but counted everything as a passing breath and lived that way; and the Lord tested them often, and their spirits were found pure, so that they might bless his name.

I have recounted in the books all the blessings meant for them. He has assigned them their reward, because they have been found to love heaven more than their life in the world. Though they were trampled by wicked people, and suffered abuse and insult from them and were put to shame, still they blessed me.{c}

Now I will call out the spirits of the good who belong to the generation of light, and I will change those who were born in darkness, who in the flesh did not receive the honor that their faithfulness earned.
I will lead them out into radiant light, those who loved my holy name, and I will set each of them on his throne of honor.
They will shine for times without number; for righteousness is God’s judgment, and to the faithful he will give faithfulness in the dwelling of upright paths.
They will see those born in darkness led into darkness, while the righteous shine.
The sinners will cry out as they see them shining, and they will go where days and times are set for them.”

notes.text: Chapter 108 is a late appendix, found only in Ethiopic; nothing of it is reported among the Aramaic fragments.
The book of life: compare 47:3; Exod 32:32–33; Ps 69:28; Rev 20:12–15.
Me: the speaker shifts from the angel to God himself in verses 10–13.
